DQ-Recommender: a Deep Learning Data Quality Auditor for Text Datasets¶

Course: Mathematics for Deep Learning, Semester 2 project
Framework: Python + PyTorch (models trained from scratch), Streamlit demo
Dataset: AG News Classification Dataset (Kaggle)

Team member Student ID Contribution

Abstract¶

Most of the time in a machine learning project goes into finding and fixing problems in the data: missing values, duplicates, broken encodings, very sparse features, wrong labels and junk rows. These problems are usually found by hand and often only after a model behaves strangely. We built DQ-Recommender, a system that audits a text dataset automatically and writes a data quality report that says what is wrong, how bad it is, and which preprocessing steps to apply, in which order.

The system has three parts:

  1. a statistical profiler (missing and disguised-missing values, duplicates and near duplicates, label conflicts, bag-of-words sparsity and vocabulary coverage, encoding artifacts, length outliers, class balance, correlations);
  2. two deep learning detectors trained from scratch on AG News: a BiGRU topic classifier used as a label auditor (confident learning), and a denoising autoencoder on character n-grams that flags garbled or off-domain content;
  3. a recommender that turns the findings into severity-ranked issues, a 0 to 100 quality score across five dimensions, an ordered preprocessing plan with code, and a one-click cleaner.

Everything is packaged as a Streamlit application.

Contents¶

  1. Dataset details, business problem, data analysis and correlation

1. Details of the dataset¶

1.1 Reference¶

  • Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/amananandrai/ag-news-classification-dataset
  • Original source: AG's corpus of news articles (more than 1 million articles gathered from 2000+ sources by the ComeToMyHead academic news search engine). The 4-class benchmark version was built by Xiang Zhang, Junbo Zhao and Yann LeCun for Character-level Convolutional Networks for Text Classification (NeurIPS 2015).
  • Size: 120,000 training rows and 7,600 test rows, perfectly balanced (30,000 / 1,900 per class).
  • Columns: Class Index (1 = World, 2 = Sports, 3 = Business, 4 = Sci/Tech), Title, Description.

1.2 Business problem¶

Imagine a news aggregator (or any company that trains models on text it collects) that receives new batches of labelled articles every week from scrapers, partners and annotators. Before a batch can be used for training, somebody has to check it. In practice the batches contain:

  • missing titles or descriptions, and empty strings that df.isna() does not see,
  • duplicated stories (the same wire story from several outlets), which inflate validation scores when copies end up in both train and test,
  • broken HTML entities and markup left over from scraping (AG News itself has thousands of #39; and &lt;b&gt; fragments),
  • extremely sparse bag-of-words representations and a long tail of rare words, which decide what representation and vocabulary size to use,
  • wrong labels, and junk rows (gibberish, boilerplate, code, other languages).

The last two cannot be caught with simple rules. That is where deep learning helps: a model that has learned what a World or Sports story looks like can point at rows whose label disagrees with the text, and a model that has learned what normal news text looks like can point at rows that do not look like news at all.

Goal: given any CSV of text data, automatically detect these issues, quantify them, and recommend the preprocessing steps that fix them. The output is a data quality report and an application a data scientist can use before training.

How we measure success:

  • the classifier has to be accurate enough to be trusted as a label auditor (target: over 90% test accuracy),
  • on a benchmark with issues we inject ourselves (so we know the ground truth), the system should find most of them (recall) without flagging too many clean rows (precision / ROC-AUC),
  • the report should be actionable: every issue comes with a severity, the number of affected rows, a recommendation and code.

# simple length features, computed on the raw text
def add_length_cols(d):
    d = d.copy()
    d["title_chars"] = d["Title"].str.len()
    d["title_words"] = d["Title"].str.split().str.len()
    d["desc_chars"] = d["Description"].str.len()
    d["desc_words"] = d["Description"].str.split().str.len()
    return d

The source prefix is a small data quality finding in itself: some sources are almost exclusive to one class, so a model can partly learn who wrote the story instead of what it is about (a mild form of shortcut learning). We keep the prefix, since it is real information at prediction time, but it is something to keep in mind.

Correlation analysis¶

AG News has no numeric columns, so we build a numeric view of each row (lengths, digit / upper-case / punctuation ratios, whether there is a source prefix, number of broken entities) and correlate it with the one-hot class indicators. Pearson correlation with a 0/1 indicator is the point-biserial correlation, which tells us which surface features are related to which class.

In [10]:

    "title_chars": train_eda["title_chars"],
    "title_words": train_eda["title_words"],
    "desc_chars": train_eda["desc_chars"],
    "desc_words": train_eda["desc_words"],
    "digit_ratio": train_raw["Description"].str.count(r"\d") / train_eda["desc_chars"],
    "upper_ratio": train_raw["Description"].str.count(r"[A-Z]") / train_eda["desc_chars"],
    "punct_ratio": train_raw["Description"].str.count(r"[^\w\s]") / train_eda["desc_chars"],
    "has_source": train_eda["source"].notna().astype(int),
    "broken_entities": train_raw["Description"].str.count(r"#\d+;|quot;|&[a-z]+;"),
})
for k, name in enumerate(CLASS_NAMES):
    feat["is_" + name] = (train_raw["label"] == k).astype(int)

corr = feat.corr()
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
sns.heatmap(corr, cmap="RdBu_r", center=0, vmin=-1, vmax=1, annot=True, fmt=".2f", annot_kws={"size": 7})
plt.title("Correlation of engineered text features and class indicators")
plt.show()

Reading the heatmap: character and word counts are almost the same variable (r close to 1), so only one of them should be kept if they were used as features. Digit ratio is higher for Business (prices, percentages) and Sports (scores). The class indicators are only weakly correlated with the surface features, which means the topic is not decided by length or formatting; we need a model of the words. This is what motivates a sequence model instead of simple features.

What the manual audit tells us about the original data: there are no NaN values and the classes are perfectly balanced, but the text is far from clean. About one row in five has broken HTML entities (#39; is an apostrophe that lost its &), there are escaped tags, literal backslashes where line breaks used to be, more than a thousand repeated descriptions, rows that appear with conflicting labels, and test rows that also appear in the training set (leakage). The rest of the project automates exactly this kind of audit and adds the parts a manual audit cannot do (label noise, junk content).

2. Preprocessing¶

The preprocessing code lives in a small module, dq/text_utils.py, because the Streamlit app must apply exactly the same cleaning and tokenisation as training. The cell below writes the module; the steps are:

  1. Repair encodings: turn bare #39; / quot; into real entities, html.unescape twice (some rows are double escaped), strip tags and URLs, replace backslashes, Unicode NFKC normalisation, collapse whitespace.
  2. Tokenise: lower-case words, digits and simple contractions.
  3. Vocabulary: most frequent words with a minimum frequency; index 0 is padding and 1 is unknown.
  4. Character n-gram features: hashed 2-4 character n-grams, L2 normalised, used by the autoencoder.

%%writefile dq/text_utils.py
"""Text cleaning, tokenisation, vocabulary and character n-gram features.

Everything the models need at inference time lives here so the notebook and the
Streamlit app use exactly the same preprocessing.
"""
import html
import json
import re
import unicodedata
from collections import Counter

import numpy as np
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import HashingVectorizer

# AG News was scraped with broken HTML entities: "#39;" instead of "&#39;",
# "quot;" instead of "&quot;", and literal backslashes where line breaks were.
BARE_NUMERIC_ENTITY = re.compile(r"(?<!&)#(\d{2,4});")
BARE_NAMED_ENTITY = re.compile(r"(?<![&\w])(quot|amp|lt|gt|nbsp);", re.I)
HTML_TAG = re.compile(r"<[^>]{1,200}>")
URL = re.compile(r"(https?://\S+|www\.\S+)", re.I)
MULTI_SPACE = re.compile(r"\s+")
TOKEN = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]+(?:'[a-z]+)?")

# Patterns used by the profiler to count artifacts in the raw text.
ARTIFACT_PATTERNS = {
    "broken_html_entity": re.compile(r"(?<!&)#\d{2,4};|(?<![&\w])(?:quot|amp|lt|gt|nbsp);|&(?:#\d+|[a-z]+);", re.I),
    "html_tag": re.compile(r"<[^>]{1,200}>|&lt;[^&]{1,200}&gt;", re.I),
    "url": URL,
    "backslash": re.compile(r"\\"),
    "non_ascii": re.compile(r"[^\x00-\x7f]"),
    "repeated_punct": re.compile(r"([!?.,])\1{3,}"),
    "spreadsheet_error": re.compile(r"#(?:NAME\?|VALUE!|REF!|DIV/0!|NUM!|NULL!)"),
}


def clean_text(text):
    """Repair encoding artifacts and normalise whitespace. Keeps case and punctuation."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        return ""
    s = BARE_NUMERIC_ENTITY.sub(r"&#\1;", text)
    s = BARE_NAMED_ENTITY.sub(r"&\1;", s)
    # unescape twice because some rows are double escaped (&amp;lt;b&amp;gt;)
    s = html.unescape(html.unescape(s))
    s = HTML_TAG.sub(" ", s)
    s = URL.sub(" ", s)
    s = s.replace("\\", " ")
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", s)
    return MULTI_SPACE.sub(" ", s).strip()


def tokenize(text):
    """Lower-case word tokens (letters, digits and simple contractions)."""
    return TOKEN.findall(text.lower()) if isinstance(text, str) else []


class Vocab:
    PAD, UNK = "<pad>", "<unk>"

    def __init__(self, itos):
        self.itos = list(itos)
        self.stoi = {w: i for i, w in enumerate(self.itos)}

    @classmethod
    def build(cls, token_lists, max_size=30000, min_freq=2):
        counts = Counter()
        for toks in token_lists:
            counts.update(toks)
        words = [w for w, c in counts.most_common(max_size - 2) if c >= min_freq]
        return cls([cls.PAD, cls.UNK] + words)

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.itos)

    def encode(self, tokens, max_len):
        ids = [self.stoi.get(t, 1) for t in tokens[:max_len]]
        return ids + [0] * (max_len - len(ids))

    def encode_batch(self, texts, max_len):
        return np.array([self.encode(tokenize(t), max_len) for t in texts], dtype=np.int64)

    def oov_rate(self, tokens):
        if not tokens:
            return 1.0
        return sum(t not in self.stoi for t in tokens) / len(tokens)

    def save(self, path):
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(self.itos, f)

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path):
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return cls(json.load(f))


# Character 2-4 grams hashed into a fixed number of buckets. HashingVectorizer is
# stateless, so there is nothing to fit or pickle; the app rebuilds it identically.
CHAR_FEATURES = 4096


def char_ngram_matrix(texts):
    hv = HashingVectorizer(
        analyzer="char_wb", ngram_range=(2, 4), n_features=CHAR_FEATURES,
        alternate_sign=False, norm="l2", lowercase=True,
    )
    return hv.transform(["" if not isinstance(t, str) else t for t in texts]).astype(np.float32)

t0 = time.time()
def prepare(d):
    d = d.copy()
    d["title_clean"] = d["Title"].map(clean_text)
    d["desc_clean"] = d["Description"].map(clean_text)
    d["text"] = (d["title_clean"] + " " + d["desc_clean"]).str.strip()
    d["tokens"] = d["text"].map(tokenize)
    d["n_tokens"] = d["tokens"].str.len()
    return d

train_df = prepare(train_raw)
test_df = prepare(test_raw)
print(f"cleaned {len(train_df) + len(test_df):,} rows in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s")

Long rows are not errors here: they are longer news stories. Dropping them would throw away real data, so instead we truncate sequences at the 99th percentile of the token count. Very short rows (fewer than 5 tokens) carry almost no signal and are dropped.

The bag-of-words matrix is more than 99.9% zeros: each story uses about 30 distinct words out of tens of thousands. A one-hot / count representation is therefore very wasteful for a neural network, which is why the classifier uses a learned dense embedding (30k words to 128 dimensions). The same sparsity statistics (percentage of zeros, words needed for 95% coverage, share of words seen once) are reported by the recommender and turned into advice on vocabulary size and representation.

Normalisation. The classifier input is a sequence of word ids, so there is nothing to scale; instead we normalise inside the network with Batch Normalisation on the pooled GRU features and the hidden layer. For the autoencoder the input vectors are L2 normalised character n-gram counts, so long and short texts are on the same scale.

3. Models¶

We train both networks from scratch (option 3.1 of the instructions).

3.1 BiGRU topic classifier (the label auditor)¶

Embedding(30k, E) (E = 128 or 200, chosen in section 4) -> Dropout -> bidirectional GRU(128) -> concatenation of masked max pooling and mean pooling over time (512 values) -> BatchNorm -> Dropout -> Linear(512, 128) + ReLU -> BatchNorm -> Dropout -> Linear(128, 4).

Max pooling picks the strongest topic cue anywhere in the text, mean pooling summarises the whole text; padding positions are masked out of both.

In [25]:
class NewsClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, embed_dim=128, hidden=128, n_classes=4, dropout=0.4):
        super().__init__()
        self.config = dict(vocab_size=vocab_size, embed_dim=embed_dim, hidden=hidden,
                           n_classes=n_classes, dropout=dropout)
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim, padding_idx=0)
        self.embed_drop = nn.Dropout(dropout / 2)
        self.gru = nn.GRU(embed_dim, hidden, batch_first=True, bidirectional=True)
        self.head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.BatchNorm1d(4 * hidden),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(4 * hidden, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(128),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(128, n_classes),
        )

    def pooled(self, x):
        mask = (x != 0).unsqueeze(-1).float()
        h, _ = self.gru(self.embed_drop(self.embedding(x)))
        h_max = (h - (1 - mask) * 1e4).max(dim=1).values     # padded steps can never win the max
        h_mean = (h * mask).sum(1) / mask.sum(1).clamp(min=1)
        return torch.cat([h_max, h_mean], dim=1)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.head(self.pooled(x))


def count_params(m):
    return sum(p.numel() for p in m.parameters() if p.requires_grad)

tmp = NewsClassifier(len(vocab))
print(tmp)

3.2 Denoising autoencoder on character n-grams (the anomaly detector)¶

Input: 4,096 hashed character 2-4 gram features (L2 normalised). Encoder 4096 -> 512 -> 64 with BatchNorm, ReLU and Dropout; decoder 64 -> 512 -> 4096. During training 10% of the input is dropped (denoising), so the network has to learn the structure of normal English news text rather than copy the input. At audit time, the reconstruction error is the anomaly score: text that does not look like news (random characters, heavy typos, code, markup, product listings) reconstructs badly.

In [26]:
class CharAutoencoder(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_features=4096, hidden=512, bottleneck=64, dropout=0.2, input_noise=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.config = dict(n_features=n_features, hidden=hidden, bottleneck=bottleneck,
                           dropout=dropout, input_noise=input_noise)
        self.input_noise = nn.Dropout(input_noise)
        self.encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(n_features, hidden), nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(hidden, bottleneck), nn.BatchNorm1d(bottleneck), nn.ReLU(),
        )
        self.decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(bottleneck, hidden), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden, n_features),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.decoder(self.encoder(self.input_noise(x)))

print("autoencoder parameters: {:,}".format(count_params(CharAutoencoder())))

4. Hyperparameter tuning¶

We tune three settings: embedding size (128 or 200), dropout rate (0.3 or 0.5) and label smoothing (0 or 0.1), which gives 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 configurations. Label smoothing replaces the one-hot target with 0.925 / 0.025 (for 4 classes), which discourages over-confident predictions; that matters here because the label auditor reads the model's probabilities. The learning rate is fixed at 2e-3 and the GRU hidden size at 128. To keep it cheap, each configuration trains for 3 epochs on a 60,000-row subset and is scored on the full validation set (validation loss is always plain cross-entropy so the runs are comparable).

First, the training helpers. They play the role of Keras' fit, evaluate and predict and keep a history dictionary with the same keys Keras uses.

In [28]:
def run_epoch(model, loader, loss_fn, optimizer=None):
    """one pass over the loader. trains if an optimizer is given, otherwise just evaluates"""
    training = optimizer is not None
    model.train(training)
    total_loss, correct, seen = 0.0, 0, 0
    for xb, yb in loader:
        xb, yb = xb.to(device), yb.to(device)
        with torch.set_grad_enabled(training):
            logits = model(xb)
            loss = loss_fn(logits, yb)
            if training:
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                loss.backward()
                nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0)   # keeps GRU gradients in check
                optimizer.step()
        total_loss += loss.item() * len(yb)
        correct += (logits.argmax(1) == yb).sum().item()
        seen += len(yb)
    return total_loss / seen, correct / seen


def fit(model, train_loader, val_loader, epochs=10, lr=1e-3, patience=3, label_smoothing=0.0,
        log_dir=None, verbose=True):
    loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(label_smoothing=label_smoothing)
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=lr, weight_decay=1e-4)
    sched = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.ReduceLROnPlateau(opt, mode="min", factor=0.5, patience=1)
    writer = None
    if log_dir:
        try:
            from torch.utils.tensorboard import SummaryWriter
            writer = SummaryWriter(log_dir)
        except ImportError:
            print("tensorboard not installed, only keeping the history dict")

    history = {"loss": [], "accuracy": [], "val_loss": [], "val_accuracy": [], "lr": []}
    best_loss, best_state, bad_epochs = float("inf"), None, 0
    for ep in range(epochs):
        t0 = time.time()
        tr_loss, tr_acc = run_epoch(model, train_loader, loss_fn, opt)
        va_loss, va_acc = run_epoch(model, val_loader, nn.CrossEntropyLoss())   # plain CE so runs compare
        sched.step(va_loss)

        history["loss"].append(tr_loss)
        history["accuracy"].append(tr_acc)
        history["val_loss"].append(va_loss)
        history["val_accuracy"].append(va_acc)
        history["lr"].append(opt.param_groups[0]["lr"])
        if writer:
            writer.add_scalars("loss", {"train": tr_loss, "val": va_loss}, ep)
            writer.add_scalars("accuracy", {"train": tr_acc, "val": va_acc}, ep)
        if verbose:
            print(f"epoch {ep + 1:2d}/{epochs}  loss {tr_loss:.4f}  acc {tr_acc:.4f}  |  "
                  f"val_loss {va_loss:.4f}  val_acc {va_acc:.4f}  lr {history['lr'][-1]:.1e}  ({time.time() - t0:.1f}s)")

        # early stopping on validation loss, remember the best weights
        if va_loss < best_loss - 1e-4:
            best_loss, bad_epochs = va_loss, 0
            best_state = {k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
        else:
            bad_epochs += 1
            if bad_epochs >= patience:
                if verbose:
                    print(f"early stopping, best val_loss {best_loss:.4f}")
                break
    if writer:
        writer.close()
    model.load_state_dict(best_state)
    return history

for emb, drop, smooth in grid:

    h = fit(m, sub_dl, val_dl, epochs=3, lr=LR, patience=5, label_smoothing=smooth, verbose=False)
    best_i = int(np.argmax(h["val_accuracy"]))

    print(f"embed={emb:3d} dropout={drop} smoothing={smooth} -> val_acc {h['val_accuracy'][best_i]:.4f}")
    del m
run_stats["tuning_seconds"] = time.time() - t0

tuning = pd.DataFrame(results).sort_values("val_acc", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)

5. Training and tracking loss / accuracy¶

The final classifier uses the best configuration and is trained on the full training split for up to 10 epochs with early stopping (patience 3 on validation loss), ReduceLROnPlateau and gradient clipping. Losses and accuracies go into history and are also written to TensorBoard (runs/classifier, open with tensorboard --logdir runs).

5.2 Training the character autoencoder¶

The autoencoder is trained only on the (already cleaned) training texts, so it learns what clean news looks like. The validation split is used to monitor the loss and, afterwards, to set the anomaly threshold.

In [33]:
t0 = time.time()
C_tr = char_ngram_matrix(tr_df["text"].tolist())
C_va = char_ngram_matrix(va_df["text"].tolist())
print("char n-gram matrices:", C_tr.shape, C_va.shape, f"| built in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s")
print("avg non-zero features per row: {:.0f} of {}".format(C_tr.nnz / C_tr.shape[0], C_tr.shape[1]))

def sparse_batches(X, batch_size, shuffle=False):
    order = np.random.permutation(X.shape[0]) if shuffle else np.arange(X.shape[0])
    for i in range(0, len(order), batch_size):
        yield torch.from_numpy(X[order[i:i + batch_size]].toarray()).to(device)

torch.manual_seed(SEED)
ae = CharAutoencoder().to(device)
ae_opt = torch.optim.Adam(ae.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
mse = nn.MSELoss()
ae_history = {"loss": [], "val_loss": []}
AE_EPOCHS = 12
if device.type == "cuda":
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()

t0 = time.time()
for epoch in range(AE_EPOCHS):
    ae.train()
    running, batches = 0.0, 0
    for xb in sparse_batches(C_tr, 512, shuffle=True):
        loss = mse(ae(xb), xb)
        ae_opt.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        ae_opt.step()
        running += loss.item()
        batches += 1
    ae.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        val_loss = np.mean([mse(ae(xb), xb).item() for xb in sparse_batches(C_va, 2048)])
    ae_history["loss"].append(running / batches)
    ae_history["val_loss"].append(val_loss)
    print(f"epoch {epoch + 1:2d}/{AE_EPOCHS}  recon loss {running / batches:.3e}  val {val_loss:.3e}")
run_stats["autoencoder_seconds"] = time.time() - t0
if device.type == "cuda":

def recon_errors(model, X, batch_size=2048):
    model.eval()
    out = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for xb in sparse_batches(X, batch_size):
            out.append(((model(xb) - xb) ** 2).mean(1).cpu().numpy())
    return np.concatenate(out)

val_err = recon_errors(ae, C_va)
print(f"validation error: median {np.median(val_err):.3e}, 99th percentile {np.percentile(val_err, 99):.3e}")

Calibrating the anomaly score for text length¶

A first version used the raw error with a single threshold. Testing it showed a problem: short but perfectly normal texts were flagged, because a short text has few active n-grams and each one carries a large weight after L2 normalisation, so its error is naturally higher. To fix this we measure the error on clean validation rows and on shortened copies of them (3 to 11 words), split them into 20 bins by the number of active n-grams, and inside each bin turn the log error into a robust z-score (median and MAD). The anomaly threshold is the 99th percentile of that z-score on clean text.

In [36]:
rng_cal = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
short_copies = [" ".join(t.split()[:rng_cal.integers(3, 12)]) for t in va_df["text"].sample(4000, random_state=SEED)]
cal_texts = va_df["text"].tolist() + short_copies
C_cal = char_ngram_matrix(cal_texts)
cal_err = recon_errors(ae, C_cal)
cal_nnz = np.diff(C_cal.indptr)          # active n-grams per row

edges = np.unique(np.quantile(cal_nnz, np.linspace(0, 1, 21)))
bin_id = np.clip(np.searchsorted(edges, cal_nnz, side="right") - 1, 0, len(edges) - 2)
log_err = np.log(cal_err)
bin_median = np.array([np.median(log_err[bin_id == k]) for k in range(len(edges) - 1)])
bin_mad = np.array([1.4826 * np.median(np.abs(log_err[bin_id == k] - bin_median[k])) for k in range(len(edges) - 1)])

def length_adjusted_score(err, nnz, cal):
    k = np.clip(np.searchsorted(np.asarray(cal["edges"]), nnz, side="right") - 1, 0, len(cal["median"]) - 1)
    return (np.log(np.maximum(err, 1e-12)) - np.asarray(cal["median"])[k]) / np.asarray(cal["mad"])[k]

AE_CAL = {"edges": edges.tolist(), "median": bin_median.tolist(), "mad": bin_mad.tolist()}
cal_z = length_adjusted_score(cal_err, cal_nnz, AE_CAL)
AE_CAL["threshold"] = float(np.percentile(cal_z, 99))
AE_CAL["reference_quantiles"] = np.quantile(cal_z, np.linspace(0, 1, 1001)).tolist()
print(f"{len(edges) - 1} length bins | z threshold (99th pct of clean text) = {AE_CAL['threshold']:.2f}")

def ae_score(texts):
    X = char_ngram_matrix([clean_text(t) for t in texts])
    err = recon_errors(ae, X)
    return length_adjusted_score(err, np.diff(X.indptr), AE_CAL), err

6. model.predict¶

predict() returns class probabilities for raw strings: they go through the same cleaning, tokenisation and encoding as the training data.

In [37]:
def predict(model, texts, batch_size=1024):
    model.eval()
    X = torch.from_numpy(vocab.encode_batch([clean_text(t) for t in texts], MAX_LEN))
    probs = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for i in range(0, len(X), batch_size):
            probs.append(torch.softmax(model(X[i:i + batch_size].to(device)), dim=1).cpu().numpy())
    return np.concatenate(probs)

8.2 The recommender modules¶

The same model classes are written to dq/models.py so the application can import them. Loading the saved weights into the module's classes below also checks that the two definitions are identical.

In [43]:
%%writefile dq/models.py
"""PyTorch models used by the data quality checks."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn


class NewsClassifier(nn.Module):
    """Embedding -> BiGRU -> (max + mean pooling) -> BatchNorm/Dropout MLP -> 4 classes.

    Trained from scratch on AG News. Inside the recommender it is used to find rows whose
    label disagrees confidently with the text (likely label noise).
    """

    def __init__(self, vocab_size, embed_dim=128, hidden=128, n_classes=4, dropout=0.4):
        super().__init__()
        self.config = dict(vocab_size=vocab_size, embed_dim=embed_dim, hidden=hidden,
                           n_classes=n_classes, dropout=dropout)
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim, padding_idx=0)
        self.embed_drop = nn.Dropout(dropout / 2)
        self.gru = nn.GRU(embed_dim, hidden, batch_first=True, bidirectional=True)
        self.head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.BatchNorm1d(4 * hidden),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(4 * hidden, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(128),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(128, n_classes),
        )

    def pooled(self, x):
        mask = (x != 0).unsqueeze(-1).float()
        h, _ = self.gru(self.embed_drop(self.embedding(x)))
        # max pooling ignores padding by pushing padded steps to a large negative value
        h_max = (h - (1 - mask) * 1e4).max(dim=1).values
        h_mean = (h * mask).sum(1) / mask.sum(1).clamp(min=1)
        return torch.cat([h_max, h_mean], dim=1)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.head(self.pooled(x))


class CharAutoencoder(nn.Module):
    """Denoising autoencoder over hashed character n-gram vectors.

    It learns what normal news text looks like at the character level. Rows it cannot
    reconstruct well (high error) are garbled, heavily misspelled or off-domain.
    """

    def __init__(self, n_features=4096, hidden=512, bottleneck=64, dropout=0.2, input_noise=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.config = dict(n_features=n_features, hidden=hidden, bottleneck=bottleneck,
                           dropout=dropout, input_noise=input_noise)
        self.input_noise = nn.Dropout(input_noise)
        self.encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(n_features, hidden),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(hidden, bottleneck),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(bottleneck),
            nn.ReLU(),
        )
        self.decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(bottleneck, hidden),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden, n_features),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.decoder(self.encoder(self.input_noise(x)))


def reconstruction_error(model, x):
    """Per-row mean squared reconstruction error (model must be in eval mode)."""
    with torch.no_grad():
        return ((model(x) - x) ** 2).mean(dim=1)

Statistical profiler (dq/profiler.py): per column it counts NaN, blank strings and placeholder tokens (n/a, null, ...), unique values, constant / ID-like columns, numeric outliers (IQR) and skew, text lengths, very short texts, ALL-CAPS rows and artifacts. Across the dataset it finds exact duplicates, normalised-text duplicates, conflicting labels, near duplicates (TF-IDF cosine >= 0.9 with nearest neighbours), bag-of-words sparsity, vocabulary coverage and OOV rate, class balance (imbalance ratio, normalised entropy) and correlations.

In [45]:
%%writefile dq/profiler.py
"""Statistical data quality profiler.

profile_dataset() returns a nested dict describing completeness, duplicates, sparsity,
text artifacts, outliers, label health and correlations. The recommender turns this
dict (plus the deep learning checks) into issues and preprocessing recommendations.
"""
import re

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer, TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors

from .text_utils import ARTIFACT_PATTERNS, tokenize

PLACEHOLDERS = {"nan", "null", "none", "n/a", "na", "-", "--", "?", "missing", "undefined", "#n/a"}
LABEL_NAME_HINTS = re.compile(r"(label|class|target|category|topic|y$)", re.I)
NORMALISE = r"[^a-z0-9 ]+"


def rx_contains(s, rx):
    """Python-regex version of str.contains (pyarrow's RE2 has no look-behind or back-references)."""
    return s.map(lambda t: isinstance(t, str) and rx.search(t) is not None).astype(bool)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- column typing
def is_text_like(s):
    return not (pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(s) or pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(s)
                or pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(s))


def detect_text_columns(df):
    cols = []
    for c in df.columns:
        s = df[c]
        if not is_text_like(s):
            continue
        vals = s.dropna().astype(str)
        if len(vals) == 0:
            continue
        if vals.str.len().median() >= 25 and vals.nunique() / len(vals) > 0.3:
            cols.append(c)
    return cols


def detect_label_column(df, text_cols):
    n = len(df)
    candidates = []
    for c in df.columns:
        if c in text_cols:
            continue
        nun = df[c].nunique(dropna=True)
        if 2 <= nun <= 50 and nun <= max(2, 0.05 * n):
            candidates.append((0 if LABEL_NAME_HINTS.search(str(c)) else 1, nun, c))
    return sorted(candidates)[0][2] if candidates else None


def column_kind(s, text_cols, label_col):
    if s.name == label_col:
        return "label"
    if s.name in text_cols:
        return "text"
    if pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(s):
        return "boolean"
    if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(s):
        return "numeric"
    if pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(s):
        return "datetime"
    return "categorical"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- missing values
def missing_masks(s):
    """Return (nan_mask, blank_mask, placeholder_mask) for a column."""
    nan = s.isna()
    if is_text_like(s):
        as_str = s.astype(str).where(~nan, "")
        stripped = as_str.str.strip()
        blank = (~nan) & (stripped == "")
        placeholder = (~nan) & (~blank) & stripped.str.lower().isin(PLACEHOLDERS)
    else:
        blank = pd.Series(False, index=s.index)
        placeholder = pd.Series(False, index=s.index)
    return nan, blank, placeholder


def any_missing_mask(df):
    mask = pd.Series(False, index=df.index)
    for c in df.columns:
        nan, blank, placeholder = missing_masks(df[c])
        mask |= nan | blank | placeholder
    return mask


def iqr_bounds(x, k=1.5):
    q1, q3 = np.nanpercentile(x, [25, 75])
    iqr = q3 - q1
    return q1 - k * iqr, q3 + k * iqr


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- per column
def profile_column(s, kind):
    n = len(s)
    nan, blank, placeholder = missing_masks(s)
    missing = nan | blank | placeholder
    p = {
        "name": str(s.name), "kind": kind, "dtype": str(s.dtype),
        "missing_nan": int(nan.sum()), "missing_blank": int(blank.sum()),
        "missing_placeholder": int(placeholder.sum()), "missing_total": int(missing.sum()),
        "missing_pct": float(missing.mean() * 100) if n else 0.0,
        "n_unique": int(s[~missing].nunique()),
    }
    valid = s[~missing]
    p["unique_ratio"] = float(p["n_unique"] / max(len(valid), 1))
    p["is_constant"] = p["n_unique"] <= 1 and len(valid) > 0

    if kind == "numeric":
        x = pd.to_numeric(valid, errors="coerce").dropna().astype(float)
        if len(x):
            lo, hi = iqr_bounds(x)
            p.update(mean=float(x.mean()), std=float(x.std()), min=float(x.min()), max=float(x.max()),
                     zeros_pct=float((x == 0).mean() * 100), skew=float(x.skew()) if len(x) > 2 else 0.0,
                     outliers_iqr=int(((x < lo) | (x > hi)).sum()))
    elif kind == "text":
        txt = valid.astype(str)
        chars = txt.str.len()
        words = txt.str.split().str.len()
        lo, hi = iqr_bounds(chars) if len(chars) else (0, 0)
        letters = txt.str.count(r"[A-Za-z]")
        upper = txt.str.count(r"[A-Z]")
        p.update(
            char_len_mean=float(chars.mean()) if len(chars) else 0.0,
            char_len_median=float(chars.median()) if len(chars) else 0.0,
            char_len_p95=float(chars.quantile(0.95)) if len(chars) else 0.0,
            word_len_mean=float(words.mean()) if len(words) else 0.0,
            word_len_p95=float(words.quantile(0.95)) if len(words) else 0.0,
            very_short=int((words < 3).sum()),
            length_outliers_low=int((chars < lo).sum()),
            length_outliers_high=int((chars > hi).sum()),
            shouting=int(((upper / letters.clip(lower=1)) > 0.7).where(letters > 10, False).sum()),
            duplicated_values=int(txt.duplicated().sum()),
            artifacts={k: int(rx_contains(txt, rx).sum()) for k, rx in ARTIFACT_PATTERNS.items()},
        )
    elif kind in ("categorical", "label"):
        vc = valid.astype(str).value_counts()
        p["top_values"] = {str(k): int(v) for k, v in vc.head(10).items()}
        p["looks_like_id"] = kind == "categorical" and p["unique_ratio"] > 0.95 and len(valid) > 50
    return p


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- dataset level
def combined_text(df, text_cols):
    if not text_cols:
        return pd.Series("", index=df.index)
    parts = [df[c].where(df[c].notna(), "").astype(str) for c in text_cols]
    out = parts[0]
    for part in parts[1:]:
        out = out + " " + part
    return out.str.strip()


def normalised_text(texts):
    return texts.str.lower().str.replace(NORMALISE, " ", regex=True).str.split().str.join(" ")


def text_sparsity(texts, vocab=None):
    """Bag-of-words sparsity, vocabulary size and coverage statistics."""
    texts = texts[texts.str.len() > 0]
    if len(texts) == 0:
        return {}
    cv = CountVectorizer(tokenizer=tokenize, lowercase=False, token_pattern=None)
    X = cv.fit_transform(texts)
    n, v = X.shape
    freqs = np.asarray(X.sum(axis=0)).ravel()
    order = np.sort(freqs)[::-1]
    cum = np.cumsum(order) / order.sum()
    out = {
        "rows": int(n), "vocab_size": int(v), "nnz": int(X.nnz),
        "sparsity_pct": float(100 * (1 - X.nnz / (n * v))),
        "avg_unique_tokens_per_row": float(X.nnz / n),
        "hapax_pct": float(100 * (freqs == 1).mean()),
        "vocab_for_90pct_coverage": int(np.searchsorted(cum, 0.90) + 1),
        "vocab_for_95pct_coverage": int(np.searchsorted(cum, 0.95) + 1),
        "coverage_curve": [(int(k), float(cum[k - 1])) for k in
                           sorted(set(np.unique(np.geomspace(1, v, 60).astype(int))))],
        "top_tokens": {w: int(c) for w, c in sorted(zip(cv.get_feature_names_out(), freqs),
                                                     key=lambda t: -t[1])[:25]},
    }
    if vocab is not None:
        oov = texts.map(lambda t: vocab.oov_rate(tokenize(t)))
        out["mean_oov_pct"] = float(oov.mean() * 100)
        out["high_oov_rows"] = [int(i) for i in oov.index[oov > 0.3]]
    return out


def near_duplicates(texts, max_rows=5000, threshold=0.9, seed=0):
    """Pairs of different texts with TF-IDF cosine similarity >= threshold (on a sample)."""
    texts = texts[texts.str.len() > 0].drop_duplicates()
    if len(texts) < 3:
        return {"checked_rows": int(len(texts)), "pairs": []}
    if len(texts) > max_rows:
        texts = texts.sample(max_rows, random_state=seed)
    X = TfidfVectorizer(tokenizer=tokenize, lowercase=False, token_pattern=None).fit_transform(texts)
    nn_ = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=2, metric="cosine").fit(X)
    dist, idx = nn_.kneighbors(X)
    pairs, seen = [], set()
    for i in range(len(texts)):
        j, sim = idx[i, 1], 1 - dist[i, 1]
        key = tuple(sorted((i, j)))
        if sim >= threshold and key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            pairs.append((int(texts.index[i]), int(texts.index[j]), float(sim)))
    return {"checked_rows": int(len(texts)), "pairs": pairs}


def label_profile(labels, valid_labels=None):
    nan, blank, placeholder = missing_masks(labels)
    missing = nan | blank | placeholder
    vals = labels[~missing].astype(str)
    out = {"missing": int(missing.sum()), "missing_rows": [int(i) for i in labels.index[missing]]}
    if valid_labels is not None:
        allowed = {str(v) for v in valid_labels}
        bad = ~vals.isin(allowed)
        out["invalid"] = int(bad.sum())
        out["invalid_rows"] = [int(i) for i in vals.index[bad]]
        out["invalid_values"] = sorted(vals[bad].unique().tolist())[:20]
        vals = vals[~bad]
    counts = vals.value_counts()
    out["counts"] = {str(k): int(v) for k, v in counts.items()}
    if len(counts) >= 2:
        p = counts / counts.sum()
        out["imbalance_ratio"] = float(counts.max() / counts.min())
        out["norm_entropy"] = float(-(p * np.log(p)).sum() / np.log(len(p)))
        out["rare_classes"] = [str(k) for k, v in p.items() if v < 0.01]
    else:
        out.update(imbalance_ratio=1.0, norm_entropy=1.0, rare_classes=[])
    return out


def engineered_features(df, text_cols):
    """Numeric view of text columns so correlations can be computed for text data too."""
    feats = pd.DataFrame(index=df.index)
    for c in text_cols:
        s = df[c].where(df[c].notna(), "").astype(str)
        feats[f"{c}__chars"] = s.str.len()
        feats[f"{c}__words"] = s.str.split().str.len()
        feats[f"{c}__digit_ratio"] = s.str.count(r"\d") / s.str.len().clip(lower=1)
        feats[f"{c}__upper_ratio"] = s.str.count(r"[A-Z]") / s.str.len().clip(lower=1)
        feats[f"{c}__punct_ratio"] = s.str.count(r"[^\w\s]") / s.str.len().clip(lower=1)
    return feats


def correlations(df, text_cols, threshold=0.95):
    num = df.select_dtypes(include="number")
    frame = pd.concat([num, engineered_features(df, text_cols)], axis=1)
    frame = frame.loc[:, frame.nunique() > 1]
    if frame.shape[1] < 2:
        return {"matrix": None, "high_pairs": []}
    corr = frame.corr(numeric_only=True)
    pairs = []
    cols = corr.columns
    for i in range(len(cols)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(cols)):
            r = corr.iloc[i, j]
            if abs(r) >= threshold:
                pairs.append((cols[i], cols[j], float(r)))
    return {"matrix": corr, "high_pairs": pairs}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- main entry point
def profile_dataset(df, text_cols=None, label_col=None, valid_labels=None, vocab=None,
                    near_dup_rows=5000):
    df = df.reset_index(drop=True)
    text_cols = [c for c in (text_cols if text_cols is not None else detect_text_columns(df)) if c in df]
    if label_col is None:
        label_col = detect_label_column(df, text_cols)
    elif label_col not in df:
        label_col = None

    n_rows, n_cols = df.shape
    cols = {c: profile_column(df[c], column_kind(df[c], text_cols, label_col)) for c in df.columns}
    missing_cells = sum(p["missing_total"] for p in cols.values())

    text = combined_text(df, text_cols)
    norm = normalised_text(text)
    has_text = norm.str.len() > 0
    dup_text_mask = norm.duplicated(keep=False) & has_text

    result = {
        "n_rows": int(n_rows), "n_cols": int(n_cols),
        "memory_mb": float(df.memory_usage(deep=True).sum() / 1e6),
        "text_cols": list(text_cols), "label_col": label_col,
        "columns": cols,
        "missing_cells": int(missing_cells),
        "missing_cells_pct": float(100 * missing_cells / max(n_rows * n_cols, 1)),
        "rows_with_missing": int(any_missing_mask(df).sum()),
        "duplicate_rows": int(df.duplicated().sum()),
        "duplicate_text_rows": int((norm.duplicated() & has_text).sum()),
        "empty_text_rows": [int(i) for i in norm.index[~has_text]] if text_cols else [],
    }

    if text_cols:
        # a duplicate text only counts as a conflict if the copies disagree on the label
        conflicts = []
        if label_col is not None:
            grp = pd.DataFrame({"t": norm[dup_text_mask], "y": df.loc[dup_text_mask, label_col].astype(str)})
            n_labels = grp.groupby("t")["y"].nunique()
            bad_texts = set(n_labels.index[n_labels > 1])
            conflicts = [int(i) for i in grp.index[grp["t"].isin(bad_texts)]]
        result["conflicting_label_rows"] = conflicts
        words = text.str.split().str.len()
        result["combined_word_p95"] = float(words[has_text].quantile(0.95)) if has_text.any() else 0.0
        # a long-form column (median >= 10 words) holding < 3 words looks truncated
        short = (words < 3) & has_text
        for c in text_cols:
            if cols[c].get("word_len_mean", 0) >= 10:
                w = df[c].where(df[c].notna(), "").astype(str).str.split().str.len()
                short |= (w > 0) & (w < 3)
        result["very_short_rows"] = [int(i) for i in short.index[short]]
        result["text_sparsity"] = text_sparsity(text, vocab)
        result["near_duplicates"] = near_duplicates(text, max_rows=near_dup_rows)
        artifact_rows = pd.Series(False, index=df.index)
        for c in text_cols:
            s = df[c].where(df[c].notna(), "").astype(str)
            for rx in ARTIFACT_PATTERNS.values():
                artifact_rows |= rx_contains(s, rx)
        result["artifact_rows"] = int(artifact_rows.sum())

    numeric_cols = [c for c, p in cols.items() if p["kind"] == "numeric"]
    if numeric_cols:
        num = df[numeric_cols].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
        result["numeric_zero_sparsity_pct"] = float(100 * ((num == 0) | num.isna()).to_numpy().mean())

    if label_col is not None:
        result["label"] = label_profile(df[label_col], valid_labels)

    result["correlation"] = correlations(df, text_cols)
    return result

Overwriting dq/profiler.py

Deep learning checks (dq/dl_checks.py).

Label noise, confident learning. For every class $j$ we compute the threshold $t_j$ = the mean predicted probability of class $j$ over the rows labelled $j$. A row with given label $y$ is flagged when another class $k \neq y$ receives $p_k \geq t_k$, meaning the model is as confident about $k$ as it normally is on genuine $k$ rows. Per-class thresholds adapt to classes the model is naturally less sure about (Business vs Sci/Tech), which a single global cut-off would not. Rows are ranked by the margin $p_k - p_y$. Rows with fewer than 12 tokens (for example a title with no description) are not judged: there is too little text to decide the topic, and those rows are already caught by the completeness checks.

Anomalies. A row is flagged when its length-adjusted reconstruction z-score is above the 99th percentile of clean validation text (section 5.2). The app also reports each row's percentile against that reference distribution. The vocabulary OOV rate from the profiler complements it: rows where more than 30% of the tokens are unknown are flagged as garbled.

%%writefile dq/dl_checks.py
"""Deep learning based quality checks: label noise and content anomalies."""
import json
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch

from .models import CharAutoencoder, NewsClassifier, reconstruction_error
from .text_utils import Vocab, char_ngram_matrix, clean_text, tokenize

LABEL_ALIASES = {
    "world": 0, "sports": 1, "sport": 1, "business": 2,
    "sci/tech": 3, "sci-tech": 3, "scitech": 3, "science": 3, "technology": 3, "tech": 3,
}


def length_adjusted_score(err, nnz, cal):
    """Robust z-score of log reconstruction error within the text-length bin.

    Short texts have few active n-grams, each carrying a large weight after L2
    normalisation, so their raw error is naturally higher. Comparing each row with clean
    rows of similar length removes that bias.
    """
    edges, med, mad = (np.asarray(cal[k]) for k in ("edges", "median", "mad"))
    k = np.clip(np.searchsorted(edges, nnz, side="right") - 1, 0, len(med) - 1)
    return (np.log(np.maximum(err, 1e-12)) - med[k]) / mad[k]


class DLChecker:
    """Loads the trained artifacts and runs both deep learning checks."""

    def __init__(self, artifact_dir="artifacts", device=None):
        self.device = device or ("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
        with open(os.path.join(artifact_dir, "config.json"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            self.config = json.load(f)
        self.vocab = Vocab.load(os.path.join(artifact_dir, "vocab.json"))
        self.class_names = self.config["class_names"]
        self.max_len = self.config["max_len"]

        self.classifier = NewsClassifier(**self.config["classifier"]).to(self.device)
        self.classifier.load_state_dict(torch.load(os.path.join(artifact_dir, "classifier.pt"),
                                                   map_location=self.device))
        self.classifier.eval()

        self.autoencoder = CharAutoencoder(**self.config["autoencoder"]).to(self.device)
        self.autoencoder.load_state_dict(torch.load(os.path.join(artifact_dir, "autoencoder.pt"),
                                                    map_location=self.device))
        self.autoencoder.eval()
        self.ae_cal = self.config["ae_calibration"]
        self.ae_threshold = self.ae_cal["threshold"]
        self.ae_reference = np.array(self.ae_cal["reference_quantiles"])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ labels
    def map_labels(self, labels):
        """Map user labels onto the 4 AG News classes. Returns (index array, ok mask) or None."""
        s = labels.astype(str).str.strip().str.lower().str.replace(r"\.0$", "", regex=True)
        s = s[labels.notna()].reindex(labels.index)
        present = s.dropna()
        if present.empty:
            return None
        # decide the encoding from the majority of values, so a few bad labels
        # ("unknown", 0, 5) do not switch the whole check off
        share = lambda allowed: present.isin(allowed).mean()
        if share({"1", "2", "3", "4"}) >= 0.9 and not (present == "0").mean() > 0.05:
            idx = pd.to_numeric(s.where(s.isin({"1", "2", "3", "4"})), errors="coerce") - 1
        elif share({"0", "1", "2", "3"}) >= 0.9:
            idx = pd.to_numeric(s.where(s.isin({"0", "1", "2", "3"})), errors="coerce")
        elif share(set(LABEL_ALIASES)) >= 0.5:
            idx = s.map(LABEL_ALIASES)
        else:
            return None
        ok = idx.notna() & idx.isin([0, 1, 2, 3])
        return idx.fillna(-1).astype(int).to_numpy(), ok.to_numpy()

    def predict_proba(self, texts, batch_size=512):
        cleaned = [clean_text(t) for t in texts]
        probs = []
        with torch.no_grad():
            for i in range(0, len(cleaned), batch_size):
                x = torch.from_numpy(self.vocab.encode_batch(cleaned[i:i + batch_size], self.max_len))
                probs.append(torch.softmax(self.classifier(x.to(self.device)), dim=1).cpu().numpy())
        return np.concatenate(probs) if probs else np.zeros((0, len(self.class_names)))

    def label_noise(self, texts, labels, min_tokens=12):
        """Confident-learning style check.

        For each class j the threshold t_j is the average probability the model gives to
        class j on rows labelled j. A row labelled y is suspicious when some other class k
        gets p_k >= t_k, i.e. the model is as sure about k as it usually is about real k rows.
        """
        mapped = self.map_labels(pd.Series(labels))
        if mapped is None:
            return None
        y, ok = mapped
        texts = pd.Series(texts).reset_index(drop=True).fillna("").astype(str)
        # too little text to judge a topic (e.g. title only): leave those to the other checks
        n_tokens = texts.map(lambda t: len(tokenize(clean_text(t)))).to_numpy()
        rows = np.where(ok & (n_tokens >= min_tokens))[0]
        if len(rows) == 0:
            return None
        P = self.predict_proba(texts.iloc[rows].tolist())
        yg = y[rows]
        k = len(self.class_names)
        thresholds = np.array([P[yg == j, j].mean() if (yg == j).any() else 1.0 for j in range(k)])
        P_other = P.copy()
        P_other[np.arange(len(rows)), yg] = -1
        above = P_other >= thresholds[None, :]
        pred = np.where(above.any(1), np.where(above, P_other, -1).argmax(1), P.argmax(1))
        flagged = above.any(1)
        out = pd.DataFrame({
            "row": rows,
            "given_label": [self.class_names[j] for j in yg],
            "predicted_label": [self.class_names[j] for j in P.argmax(1)],
            "suggested_label": [self.class_names[j] for j in pred],
            "p_given": P[np.arange(len(rows)), yg],
            "p_suggested": P[np.arange(len(rows)), pred],
            "flagged": flagged,
        })
        out["margin"] = out["p_suggested"] - out["p_given"]
        out.attrs["thresholds"] = {c: round(float(t), 3) for c, t in zip(self.class_names, thresholds)}
        out.attrs["accuracy_vs_given"] = float((P.argmax(1) == yg).mean())
        out.attrs["skipped_short"] = int((ok & (n_tokens < min_tokens)).sum())
        return out

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ anomalies
    def anomaly_scores(self, texts, batch_size=1024):
        """Raw reconstruction error, number of active n-grams and length-adjusted z-score."""
        cleaned = [clean_text(t) for t in texts]
        X = char_ngram_matrix(cleaned)
        errs = []
        for i in range(0, X.shape[0], batch_size):
            xb = torch.from_numpy(X[i:i + batch_size].toarray()).to(self.device)
            errs.append(reconstruction_error(self.autoencoder, xb).cpu().numpy())
        err = np.concatenate(errs) if errs else np.zeros(0)
        nnz = np.diff(X.indptr)
        return err, nnz, length_adjusted_score(err, nnz, self.ae_cal)

    def anomalies(self, texts):
        texts = pd.Series(texts).reset_index(drop=True).fillna("").astype(str)
        has_text = texts.str.strip().str.len() > 0
        rows = np.where(has_text.to_numpy())[0]
        if len(rows) == 0:
            return None
        err, nnz, z = self.anomaly_scores(texts.iloc[rows].tolist())
        pct = np.searchsorted(self.ae_reference, z) / max(len(self.ae_reference) - 1, 1) * 100
        return pd.DataFrame({
            "row": rows, "recon_error": err, "n_ngrams": nnz, "anomaly_z": z,
            "reference_percentile": np.clip(pct, 0, 100), "flagged": z > self.ae_threshold,
        })

Recommender (dq/recommender.py): each finding becomes an Issue with a category, a severity (critical / high / medium / low / info, from the share of affected rows), the number of affected rows, a recommendation, a code snippet and its place in the preprocessing pipeline. The quality score combines five dimensions:

Dimension Based on Weight
Completeness share of missing cells (NaN + blank + placeholder) 0.30
Uniqueness duplicate and near-duplicate rows 0.20
Validity artifacts, very short texts, OOV-dominated rows, DL anomalies, outliers 0.30
Label quality missing/invalid labels, conflicts, DL-suspected mislabels 0.25
Balance normalised entropy of the class distribution 0.10

(weights are renormalised when there is no label column). The report is rendered as Markdown and as a standalone HTML page.

%%writefile dq/recommender.py
"""Turns profiler + deep learning findings into scored issues and preprocessing advice."""
import html as htmllib
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime

import numpy as np

SEVERITY_ORDER = {"critical": 0, "high": 1, "medium": 2, "low": 3, "info": 4}
SEVERITY_COLOR = {"critical": "#b42318", "high": "#c4320a", "medium": "#b54708", "low": "#475467", "info": "#1d4ed8"}


@dataclass
class Issue:
    id: str
    category: str
    title: str
    severity: str
    affected: int
    pct: float
    detail: str
    recommendation: str
    code: str = ""
    step: int = 99          # position in the recommended preprocessing pipeline
    rows: list = field(default_factory=list)


def severity_from_pct(pct, critical=20, high=5, medium=1):
    if pct >= critical:
        return "critical"
    if pct >= high:
        return "high"
    if pct >= medium:
        return "medium"
    return "low"


def _pct(k, n):
    return 100.0 * k / max(n, 1)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- rules
def build_issues(profile, label_noise=None, anomalies=None):
    n = profile["n_rows"]
    issues = []
    add = issues.append
    text_cols = profile["text_cols"]
    label_col = profile.get("label_col")

    # 1. completeness -------------------------------------------------------
    for name, c in profile["columns"].items():
        if c["missing_total"] == 0:
            continue
        pct = c["missing_pct"]
        parts = []
        if c["missing_nan"]:
            parts.append(f"{c['missing_nan']} NaN")
        if c["missing_blank"]:
            parts.append(f"{c['missing_blank']} empty/whitespace strings")
        if c["missing_placeholder"]:
            parts.append(f"{c['missing_placeholder']} placeholder tokens (e.g. 'n/a', 'null')")
        if c["kind"] == "text":
            others = [t for t in text_cols if t != name]
            rec = (f"Text cannot be imputed meaningfully. Fill missing '{name}' with an empty string and "
                   f"rely on {', '.join(repr(o) for o in others)} for those rows; drop rows where every text field is empty."
                   if others else f"Drop rows where '{name}' is missing; it is the only model input.")
            code = f"df['{name}'] = df['{name}'].replace(r'^\\s*$', np.nan, regex=True).fillna('')"
        elif c["kind"] == "numeric":
            rec = ("Impute with the median (robust to outliers) and add a missing-indicator column; "
                   "use KNN/iterative imputation if the column is important." if pct < 40 else
                   "More than 40% missing: consider dropping the column or modelling missingness explicitly.")
            code = f"df['{name}_was_missing'] = df['{name}'].isna()\ndf['{name}'] = df['{name}'].fillna(df['{name}'].median())"
        elif c["kind"] == "label":
            rec = "Rows without a label cannot be used for supervised training: drop them or send them for annotation."
            code = f"df = df.dropna(subset=['{label_col}'])"
        else:
            rec = "Impute with the mode or an explicit 'Unknown' category."
            code = f"df['{name}'] = df['{name}'].fillna('Unknown')"
        add(Issue(f"missing_{name}", "Completeness", f"Missing values in '{name}'",
                  severity_from_pct(pct, 30, 5, 0.5), c["missing_total"], pct,
                  "; ".join(parts) + ".", rec, code, step=1))
        if c["missing_blank"] or c["missing_placeholder"]:
            add(Issue(f"disguised_missing_{name}", "Completeness", f"Disguised missing values in '{name}'",
                      "medium", c["missing_blank"] + c["missing_placeholder"],
                      _pct(c["missing_blank"] + c["missing_placeholder"], n),
                      "Empty strings or placeholder tokens are not counted by df.isna(), so they slip past naive checks.",
                      "Convert blanks and placeholder tokens to real NaN before any other step.",
                      "df = df.replace(r'^\\s*$', np.nan, regex=True)\n"
                      "df = df.replace({'n/a': np.nan, 'null': np.nan, 'none': np.nan, '?': np.nan})", step=0))

    if profile.get("empty_text_rows"):
        k = len(profile["empty_text_rows"])
        add(Issue("empty_text", "Completeness", "Rows with no usable text", severity_from_pct(_pct(k, n), 10, 2, 0.2),
                  k, _pct(k, n), "Every text column is empty for these rows, so they carry no signal.",
                  "Drop these rows.", "df = df[df[TEXT_COLS].fillna('').apply(' '.join, axis=1).str.strip() != '']",
                  step=2, rows=profile["empty_text_rows"][:500]))

    # 2. uniqueness ---------------------------------------------------------
    if profile["duplicate_rows"]:
        k = profile["duplicate_rows"]
        add(Issue("dup_rows", "Uniqueness", "Exact duplicate rows", severity_from_pct(_pct(k, n), 10, 2, 0.2), k, _pct(k, n),
                  "Identical rows inflate the weight of some examples and leak between train and test splits.",
                  "Drop exact duplicates, keeping the first occurrence.", "df = df.drop_duplicates()", step=4))
    extra_dup = profile.get("duplicate_text_rows", 0) - profile["duplicate_rows"]
    if extra_dup > 0:
        add(Issue("dup_text", "Uniqueness", "Duplicate text (after normalisation)", severity_from_pct(_pct(extra_dup, n), 10, 2, 0.5),
                  extra_dup, _pct(extra_dup, n),
                  "Same text up to case/punctuation but differing in other fields.",
                  "Deduplicate on the normalised text; if labels differ see the label-conflict issue.",
                  "key = df[TEXT_COLS].fillna('').apply(' '.join, axis=1).str.lower().str.replace(r'[^a-z0-9 ]', '', regex=True)\n"
                  "df = df[~key.duplicated()]", step=4))
    nd = profile.get("near_duplicates", {})
    if nd.get("pairs"):
        k, checked = len(nd["pairs"]), nd["checked_rows"]
        add(Issue("near_dup", "Uniqueness", "Near-duplicate texts (TF-IDF cosine >= 0.9)", severity_from_pct(_pct(k, checked), 10, 2, 0.5),
                  k, _pct(k, checked),
                  f"{k} near-duplicate pairs among {checked} sampled rows (rewrites or minor edits of the same story).",
                  "Remove near duplicates or keep them in the same split (group split) so validation scores are not inflated.",
                  "# group near-duplicates and split by group\nfrom sklearn.model_selection import GroupShuffleSplit",
                  step=5, rows=[p[0] for p in nd["pairs"]][:500]))

    # 3. validity of text ---------------------------------------------------
    max_len = int(np.ceil(profile.get("combined_word_p95", 0))) or 64
    for name in text_cols:
        c = profile["columns"][name]
        art = c.get("artifacts", {})
        labels = {"broken_html_entity": "broken HTML entities (e.g. '#39;', '&amp;')", "html_tag": "HTML tags",
                  "url": "URLs", "backslash": "stray backslashes", "non_ascii": "non-ASCII characters",
                  "repeated_punct": "repeated punctuation",
                  "spreadsheet_error": "spreadsheet error codes (e.g. #NAME?)"}
        found = {k: v for k, v in art.items() if v}
        if found:
            total = max(found.values())
            add(Issue(f"artifacts_{name}", "Validity", f"Encoding / markup artifacts in '{name}'",
                      severity_from_pct(_pct(total, n), 40, 10, 1), total, _pct(total, n),
                      "Found " + ", ".join(f"{v} rows with {labels[k]}" for k, v in found.items()) + ".",
                      "Repair entities with html.unescape (after fixing bare '#39;' style entities), strip tags/URLs, "
                      "replace backslashes with spaces and normalise unicode (NFKC).",
                      "from dq.text_utils import clean_text\nfor col in TEXT_COLS:\n    df[col] = df[col].map(clean_text)", step=3))
        if c.get("shouting"):
            k = c["shouting"]
            add(Issue(f"shouting_{name}", "Validity", f"ALL-CAPS text in '{name}'", "low", k, _pct(k, n),
                      "Mostly upper-case rows look like headlines/boilerplate and create duplicate vocabulary entries.",
                      "Lower-case during tokenisation (already done by the recommended tokenizer).", "", step=6))
        hi = c.get("length_outliers_high", 0)
        if hi:
            add(Issue(f"len_outlier_{name}", "Validity", f"Unusually long texts in '{name}' (IQR rule)",
                      severity_from_pct(_pct(hi, n), 20, 8, 3), hi, _pct(hi, n),
                      f"95th percentile length is {c['char_len_p95']:.0f} chars / {c['word_len_p95']:.0f} words.",
                      f"Do not drop them: truncate the combined text at about {max_len} tokens (95th percentile) "
                      "and inspect the longest rows for concatenated articles.",
                      f"MAX_LEN = {max_len}", step=8))
    if profile.get("very_short_rows"):
        k = len(profile["very_short_rows"])
        add(Issue("very_short", "Validity", "Very short / truncated texts (< 3 words)", severity_from_pct(_pct(k, n), 10, 2, 0.5),
                  k, _pct(k, n), "Too little content to classify; often the result of truncation or scraping errors.",
                  "Drop or send for review.", "df = df[text.str.split().str.len() >= 3]", step=6,
                  rows=profile["very_short_rows"][:500]))

    # 4. sparsity -----------------------------------------------------------
    ts = profile.get("text_sparsity") or {}
    if ts:
        add(Issue("bow_sparsity", "Sparsity", "Bag-of-words representation is extremely sparse",
                  "info" if ts["sparsity_pct"] < 99 else "medium", ts["rows"], ts["sparsity_pct"],
                  f"{ts['sparsity_pct']:.3f}% of the {ts['rows']} x {ts['vocab_size']} document-term matrix is zero "
                  f"(about {ts['avg_unique_tokens_per_row']:.1f} distinct tokens per row). {ts['hapax_pct']:.1f}% of the "
                  f"vocabulary appears only once; {ts['vocab_for_95pct_coverage']} words cover 95% of all tokens.",
                  f"Keep sparse matrices (scipy CSR) for classic models, cap the vocabulary at about "
                  f"{ts['vocab_for_95pct_coverage']} words with min_freq >= 2, and prefer dense learned embeddings for deep models.",
                  f"TfidfVectorizer(min_df=2, max_features={ts['vocab_for_95pct_coverage']}, sublinear_tf=True)", step=7))
        if ts.get("high_oov_rows"):
            k = len(ts["high_oov_rows"])
            add(Issue("high_oov", "Validity", "Rows dominated by out-of-vocabulary tokens", severity_from_pct(_pct(k, n), 5, 1, 0.2),
                      k, _pct(k, n), f"Over 30% of the tokens are unknown to the reference vocabulary (mean OOV {ts['mean_oov_pct']:.1f}%). "
                      "Typical of gibberish, heavy typos, other languages or code.",
                      "Inspect and drop garbled rows; if the text is valid but domain-specific, extend the vocabulary.", "",
                      step=6, rows=ts["high_oov_rows"][:500]))
    if profile.get("numeric_zero_sparsity_pct", 0) > 50:
        z = profile["numeric_zero_sparsity_pct"]
        add(Issue("numeric_sparsity", "Sparsity", "Numeric features are mostly zero/missing", "medium", n, z,
                  f"{z:.1f}% of numeric cells are zero or missing.",
                  "Store as sparse, drop near-empty columns, or use models that handle sparsity (tree ensembles, linear with L1).",
                  "", step=7))

    # 5. numeric columns ----------------------------------------------------
    scales = []
    for name, c in profile["columns"].items():
        if c["kind"] == "numeric" and "std" in c:
            scales.append(c["std"])
            if c.get("outliers_iqr"):
                k = c["outliers_iqr"]
                add(Issue(f"outliers_{name}", "Validity", f"Outliers in '{name}' (IQR rule)",
                          severity_from_pct(_pct(k, n), 15, 5, 1), k, _pct(k, n),
                          f"Range {c['min']:.3g} to {c['max']:.3g}, skew {c['skew']:.2f}.",
                          "Check whether they are errors. Winsorise/clip at the 1st/99th percentile or use RobustScaler.",
                          f"lo, hi = df['{name}'].quantile([.01, .99])\ndf['{name}'] = df['{name}'].clip(lo, hi)", step=8))
            if abs(c.get("skew", 0)) > 2 and c.get("min", -1) >= 0:
                add(Issue(f"skew_{name}", "Distribution", f"Highly skewed '{name}'", "low", n, 100.0,
                          f"Skewness {c['skew']:.2f}.", "Apply log1p or Box-Cox before scaling.",
                          f"df['{name}'] = np.log1p(df['{name}'])", step=9))
        if c.get("is_constant"):
            add(Issue(f"constant_{name}", "Redundancy", f"Constant column '{name}'", "medium", n, 100.0,
                      "Only one distinct value, so it carries no information.", "Drop the column.",
                      f"df = df.drop(columns=['{name}'])", step=1))
        if c.get("looks_like_id"):
            add(Issue(f"id_{name}", "Redundancy", f"'{name}' looks like an identifier", "low", n, 100.0,
                      f"{c['unique_ratio']*100:.1f}% unique values.", "Exclude identifiers from model features.", "", step=1))
    if len(scales) >= 2 and max(scales) / max(min(scales), 1e-9) > 100:
        add(Issue("scaling", "Distribution", "Numeric features on very different scales", "medium", n, 100.0,
                  f"Standard deviations range from {min(scales):.3g} to {max(scales):.3g}.",
                  "Normalise (StandardScaler / MinMaxScaler) before training neural networks or distance-based models.",
                  "from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler", step=9))
    for a, b, r in profile.get("correlation", {}).get("high_pairs", []):
        if "__" in a and "__" in b and a.split("__")[0] == b.split("__")[0]:
            continue  # chars vs words of the same text column are expected to correlate
        add(Issue(f"corr_{a}_{b}", "Redundancy", f"'{a}' and '{b}' are highly correlated", "low", n, abs(r) * 100,
                  f"Pearson r = {r:.3f}.", "Keep one of the pair to reduce redundancy/multicollinearity.", "", step=9))

    # 6. labels -------------------------------------------------------------
    lab = profile.get("label")
    if lab:
        if lab.get("invalid"):
            k = lab["invalid"]
            add(Issue("invalid_labels", "Label quality", "Labels outside the allowed set", severity_from_pct(_pct(k, n), 5, 1, 0.1),
                      k, _pct(k, n), f"Unexpected values: {', '.join(map(str, lab['invalid_values']))}.",
                      "Map them to a valid class if the mapping is obvious, otherwise drop the rows.",
                      f"df = df[df['{label_col}'].isin(VALID_LABELS)]", step=2, rows=lab["invalid_rows"][:500]))
        ir = lab.get("imbalance_ratio", 1)
        if ir > 1.5:
            add(Issue("imbalance", "Label quality", "Class imbalance", "high" if ir > 5 else "medium" if ir > 2 else "low",
                      n, 100 * (1 - lab["norm_entropy"]),
                      f"Largest/smallest class ratio {ir:.2f}; normalised entropy {lab['norm_entropy']:.3f}. Counts: {lab['counts']}.",
                      "Use stratified splits, class weights in the loss, or re-sampling; report macro-F1 rather than accuracy.",
                      "weights = len(y) / (n_classes * np.bincount(y))\nloss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(weight=torch.tensor(weights))",
                      step=10))
        conflicts = profile.get("conflicting_label_rows", [])
        if conflicts:
            k = len(conflicts)
            add(Issue("label_conflict", "Label quality", "Same text with conflicting labels", severity_from_pct(_pct(k, n), 2, 0.5, 0.1),
                      k, _pct(k, n), "Identical (normalised) texts appear with different labels.",
                      "Resolve by majority vote or manual review; drop the group if no majority exists.", "", step=4,
                      rows=conflicts[:500]))

    if label_noise is not None and len(label_noise):
        flagged = label_noise[label_noise["flagged"]].sort_values("margin", ascending=False)
        k = len(flagged)
        if k:
            add(Issue("label_noise", "Label quality", "Likely mislabelled rows (BiGRU classifier, confident learning)",
                      severity_from_pct(_pct(k, n), 10, 3, 0.5), k, _pct(k, n),
                      f"The classifier confidently prefers another class for {k} rows "
                      f"(per-class thresholds {label_noise.attrs.get('thresholds')}; "
                      f"{label_noise.attrs.get('skipped_short', 0)} rows with under 12 tokens were not judged).",
                      "Review the top-ranked rows first. Relabel to the suggested class when correct, drop when ambiguous, "
                      "or train with a noise-robust loss (label smoothing).", "", step=11,
                      rows=flagged["row"].tolist()[:500]))
    if anomalies is not None and len(anomalies):
        flagged = anomalies[anomalies["flagged"]].sort_values("anomaly_z", ascending=False)
        k = len(flagged)
        if k:
            add(Issue("anomalies", "Validity", "Anomalous / garbled content (character autoencoder)",
                      severity_from_pct(_pct(k, n), 10, 3, 1), k, _pct(k, n),
                      "Length-adjusted reconstruction error above the 99th percentile of clean AG News text: "
                      "garbled strings, heavy typos, markup or content unlike news.",
                      "Inspect the highest-error rows; drop the garbage ones and keep genuine but unusual news.", "",
                      step=6, rows=flagged["row"].tolist()[:500]))

    issues.sort(key=lambda i: (SEVERITY_ORDER[i.severity], -i.pct))
    return issues


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- scoring
def _rows(issues, ids_prefix):
    return sum(i.affected for i in issues if any(i.id.startswith(p) for p in ids_prefix))


def quality_scores(profile, issues):
    n = max(profile["n_rows"], 1)
    completeness = 100 - profile["missing_cells_pct"]
    uniqueness = 100 - min(100, _pct(max(profile.get("duplicate_text_rows", 0), profile["duplicate_rows"]), n)
                           + (next((i.pct for i in issues if i.id == "near_dup"), 0)))
    validity = 100 - min(100, _pct(profile.get("artifact_rows", 0), n) * 0.5
                         + _pct(_rows(issues, ["very_short", "anomalies", "high_oov", "empty_text"]), n)
                         + sum(i.pct for i in issues if i.id.startswith("outliers_")) * 0.5)
    scores = {"Completeness": completeness, "Uniqueness": uniqueness, "Validity": validity}
    weights = {"Completeness": 0.3, "Uniqueness": 0.2, "Validity": 0.3}
    if profile.get("label"):
        bad = _rows(issues, ["invalid_labels", "label_conflict", "label_noise"]) + profile["label"]["missing"]
        scores["Label quality"] = 100 - min(100, _pct(bad, n) * 2)
        scores["Balance"] = 100 * profile["label"].get("norm_entropy", 1)
        weights.update({"Label quality": 0.25, "Balance": 0.1})
    total = sum(weights.values())
    overall = sum(scores[k] * weights[k] for k in scores) / total
    scores = {k: float(np.clip(v, 0, 100)) for k, v in scores.items()}
    return float(np.clip(overall, 0, 100)), scores


def grade(score):
    return "A" if score >= 90 else "B" if score >= 80 else "C" if score >= 70 else "D" if score >= 60 else "F"


def pipeline(issues):
    steps, seen = [], set()
    for i in sorted(issues, key=lambda i: (i.step, SEVERITY_ORDER[i.severity])):
        if i.severity == "info" and not i.code:
            continue
        key = (i.step, i.recommendation)
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        steps.append(i)
    return steps


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- report
def build_report(profile, label_noise=None, anomalies=None, dataset_name="dataset"):
    issues = build_issues(profile, label_noise, anomalies)
    overall, scores = quality_scores(profile, issues)
    return {
        "dataset": dataset_name,
        "generated": datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
        "overall": overall, "grade": grade(overall), "scores": scores,
        "issues": issues, "pipeline": pipeline(issues), "profile": profile,
    }


def to_markdown(report):
    p = report["profile"]
    out = [f"# Data Quality Report: {report['dataset']}",
           f"Generated {report['generated']}  ",
           f"**Overall score: {report['overall']:.1f}/100 (grade {report['grade']})**", "",
           f"Rows: {p['n_rows']:,}  Columns: {p['n_cols']}  Text columns: {', '.join(p['text_cols']) or 'none'}  "
           f"Label column: {p.get('label_col') or 'none'}", "", "## Quality dimensions", "",
           "| Dimension | Score |", "|---|---|"]
    out += [f"| {k} | {v:.1f} |" for k, v in report["scores"].items()]
    out += ["", "## Issues", "", "| Severity | Category | Issue | Affected | % |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    out += [f"| {i.severity} | {i.category} | {i.title} | {i.affected:,} | {i.pct:.2f} |" for i in report["issues"]]
    out += ["", "## Recommended preprocessing pipeline", ""]
    for k, i in enumerate(report["pipeline"], 1):
        out.append(f"{k}. **{i.title}**: {i.recommendation}")
        if i.code:
            out += ["", "```python", i.code, "```", ""]
    out += ["", "## Issue details", ""]
    for i in report["issues"]:
        out += [f"### [{i.severity.upper()}] {i.title}", i.detail, "", f"Recommendation: {i.recommendation}", ""]
    return "\n".join(out)


def to_html(report):
    e = htmllib.escape
    p = report["profile"]
    dims = "".join(
        f"<div class='dim'><div class='dname'>{e(k)}</div><div class='bar'><span style='width:{v:.1f}%'></span></div>"
        f"<div class='dval'>{v:.1f}</div></div>" for k, v in report["scores"].items())
    rows = "".join(
        f"<tr><td><span class='sev' style='background:{SEVERITY_COLOR[i.severity]}'>{i.severity}</span></td>"
        f"<td>{e(i.category)}</td><td><b>{e(i.title)}</b><div class='muted'>{e(i.detail)}</div></td>"
        f"<td class='num'>{i.affected:,}</td><td class='num'>{i.pct:.2f}%</td></tr>" for i in report["issues"])
    steps = "".join(
        f"<li><b>{e(i.title)}</b><p>{e(i.recommendation)}</p>"
        + (f"<pre>{e(i.code)}</pre>" if i.code else "") + "</li>" for i in report["pipeline"])
    cols = "".join(
        f"<tr><td>{e(c['name'])}</td><td>{e(c['kind'])}</td><td>{e(c['dtype'])}</td>"
        f"<td class='num'>{c['missing_total']:,}</td><td class='num'>{c['missing_pct']:.2f}%</td>"
        f"<td class='num'>{c['n_unique']:,}</td></tr>" for c in p["columns"].values())
    ts = p.get("text_sparsity") or {}
    sparsity = (f"<p>Document-term matrix: {ts['rows']:,} rows x {ts['vocab_size']:,} terms, "
                f"<b>{ts['sparsity_pct']:.3f}% sparse</b>. {ts['vocab_for_95pct_coverage']:,} words cover 95% of tokens; "
                f"{ts['hapax_pct']:.1f}% of words occur once.</p>") if ts else ""
    return f"""<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset='utf-8'><title>Data Quality Report</title>
<style>
body{{font-family:system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif;margin:0;background:#f6f7f9;color:#101828}}
main{{max-width:1000px;margin:auto;padding:24px 16px}}
.card{{background:#fff;border:1px solid #e4e7ec;border-radius:10px;padding:18px 20px;margin:14px 0}}
h1{{margin:0 0 4px}} h2{{margin:0 0 12px;font-size:18px}}
.score{{font-size:44px;font-weight:700}} .grade{{font-size:18px;color:#475467}}
.dim{{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;margin:6px 0}} .dname{{width:130px}}
.bar{{flex:1;background:#eaecf0;border-radius:6px;height:10px;overflow:hidden}}
.bar span{{display:block;height:100%;background:#2e7d6b}} .dval{{width:50px;text-align:right}}
table{{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;font-size:14px}} td,th{{border-bottom:1px solid #eaecf0;padding:8px;text-align:left;vertical-align:top}}
.num{{text-align:right;white-space:nowrap}} .muted{{color:#667085;font-size:13px;margin-top:3px}}
.sev{{color:#fff;border-radius:4px;padding:2px 7px;font-size:12px;text-transform:uppercase}}
pre{{background:#f2f4f7;padding:10px;border-radius:6px;overflow-x:auto;font-size:12.5px}}
li p{{margin:4px 0}}
</style></head><body><main>
<div class='card'><h1>Data Quality Report</h1><div class='muted'>{e(report['dataset'])} | generated {report['generated']}</div>
<div style='display:flex;gap:40px;align-items:center;margin-top:12px;flex-wrap:wrap'>
<div><div class='score'>{report['overall']:.1f}</div><div class='grade'>out of 100, grade {report['grade']}</div></div>
<div style='flex:1;min-width:260px'>{dims}</div></div>
<p class='muted'>{p['n_rows']:,} rows, {p['n_cols']} columns. Text: {e(', '.join(p['text_cols']) or 'none')}. Label: {e(str(p.get('label_col')))}.</p></div>
<div class='card'><h2>Issues found ({len(report['issues'])})</h2><table><tr><th>Severity</th><th>Category</th><th>Issue</th><th>Affected</th><th>%</th></tr>{rows}</table></div>
<div class='card'><h2>Recommended preprocessing pipeline</h2><ol>{steps}</ol></div>
<div class='card'><h2>Sparsity</h2>{sparsity}<p>Missing cells: {p['missing_cells']:,} ({p['missing_cells_pct']:.2f}%).</p></div>
<div class='card'><h2>Column profile</h2><table><tr><th>Column</th><th>Kind</th><th>dtype</th><th>Missing</th><th>Missing %</th><th>Unique</th></tr>{cols}</table></div>
</main></body></html>"""


def issues_frame(issues):
    import pandas as pd
    return pd.DataFrame([{k: v for k, v in asdict(i).items() if k != "rows"} for i in issues])
