%%writefile dq/cleaning.py
"""Applies the recommended preprocessing steps and logs what changed."""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from .profiler import PLACEHOLDERS, combined_text, normalised_text
from .text_utils import clean_text

DEFAULT_STEPS = ("standardise_missing", "repair_text", "drop_empty_text", "drop_invalid_labels",
                 "drop_duplicates", "drop_conflicts", "drop_short", "drop_anomalies", "fix_label_noise")


def apply_cleaning(df, profile, steps=DEFAULT_STEPS, label_noise=None, anomalies=None,
                   valid_labels=None, label_noise_action="drop"):
    df = df.reset_index(drop=True).copy()
    text_cols, label_col = profile["text_cols"], profile.get("label_col")
    log = []

    def note(step, before):
        log.append({"step": step, "rows_before": before, "rows_after": len(df), "removed": before - len(df)})

    if "standardise_missing" in steps:
        for c in df.columns:
            if df[c].dtype == object or pd.api.types.is_string_dtype(df[c]):
                s = df[c].astype("object")
                stripped = s.where(s.isna(), s.astype(str).str.strip())
                bad = stripped.isin([""]) | stripped.astype(str).str.lower().isin(PLACEHOLDERS)
                df[c] = s.mask(bad & s.notna(), np.nan)
        note("standardise_missing", len(df))

    # row-level decisions from the DL checks refer to the original row positions
    drop_rows = set()
    if "drop_anomalies" in steps:
        if anomalies is not None:
            drop_rows |= set(anomalies.loc[anomalies["flagged"], "row"].tolist())
        drop_rows |= set((profile.get("text_sparsity") or {}).get("high_oov_rows", []))
    if "drop_short" in steps:
        drop_rows |= set(profile.get("very_short_rows", []))
    if "fix_label_noise" in steps and label_noise is not None and label_col:
        flagged = label_noise[label_noise["flagged"]]
        if label_noise_action == "relabel":
            # write the suggestion in the dataset's own label encoding (1-4, 0-3 or names)
            from .agent import label_value_map
            values = label_value_map(df, label_col, label_noise)
            for r, lab in zip(flagged["row"], flagged["suggested_label"]):
                if lab in values:
                    df.at[r, label_col] = values[lab]
            log.append({"step": "relabel_label_noise", "rows_before": len(df), "rows_after": len(df),
                        "removed": 0, "relabelled": len(flagged)})
        else:
            drop_rows |= set(flagged["row"].tolist())
    if drop_rows:
        before = len(df)
        df = df.drop(index=[r for r in drop_rows if r in df.index])
        note("drop_dl_flagged_rows", before)

    if "repair_text" in steps:
        for c in text_cols:
            df[c] = df[c].map(lambda t: clean_text(t) if isinstance(t, str) else t)
        note("repair_text", len(df))

    text = combined_text(df, text_cols)
    if "drop_empty_text" in steps and text_cols:
        before = len(df)
        df = df[text.str.strip().str.len() > 0]
        note("drop_empty_text", before)

    if "drop_invalid_labels" in steps and label_col:
        before = len(df)
        keep = df[label_col].notna()
        if valid_labels is not None:
            keep &= df[label_col].astype(str).isin({str(v) for v in valid_labels})
        df = df[keep]
        note("drop_invalid_or_missing_labels", before)

    if "drop_conflicts" in steps and label_col and text_cols:
        before = len(df)
        key = normalised_text(combined_text(df, text_cols))
        n_lab = df.groupby(key)[label_col].transform("nunique")
        df = df[n_lab <= 1]
        note("drop_conflicting_labels", before)

    if "drop_duplicates" in steps:
        before = len(df)
        df = df.drop_duplicates()
        if text_cols:
            key = normalised_text(combined_text(df, text_cols))
            df = df[~key.duplicated()]
        note("drop_duplicates", before)

    if "drop_short" in steps and text_cols:
        # rows that are short only after repairing the text
        before = len(df)
        df = df[combined_text(df, text_cols).str.split().str.len() >= 3]
        note("drop_short_text", before)

    if text_cols:
        for c in text_cols:
            df[c] = df[c].fillna("")
    return df.reset_index(drop=True), pd.DataFrame(log)

Overwriting dq/cleaning.py

8.3 A benchmark with known issues¶

The original AG News has no missing values and balanced classes, so to test whether the system finds issues we inject them ourselves into the test set (which neither model has seen) and keep the ground truth. Each corruption goes into a separate set of rows:

Injected issue Share What it simulates
label flip 5% annotation mistakes
missing title (NaN) / placeholder title "N/A" 3% / 0.5% broken scraper fields
missing description (NaN) / blank description 2% / 1% empty fields, disguised missing
gibberish / heavy typos / off-domain content 2% / 2% / 1% junk rows, OCR noise, wrong source
HTML markup + URLs 2% unstripped web pages
truncated description (2 words) 1.5% cut-off records
invalid label (0, 5, "unknown", NaN) 0.5% bad label values
exact duplicates / near duplicates / duplicates with a different label 2% / 1% / 0.5% repeated stories
In [49]:
LETTERS = list("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz")
OFF_DOMAIN = [
    "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore",
    "def load(path): return [json.loads(l) for l in open(path) if l.strip()]  # TODO fix encoding",
    "SKU 44821-B | qty 12 | price 19.99 USD | color blue | size XL | warehouse 7 | in stock",
    "ERROR 0x80070005 at module kernel32.dll offset 0004f2a1 stack trace follows 0x0000 0x0001",
    "user_id,session,clicks,dwell_ms 1029,ab12,4,2300 1030,ab13,1,410 1031,ab14,9,8800",
]

def gibberish(rng):
    return " ".join("".join(rng.choice(LETTERS, rng.integers(2, 10))) for _ in range(rng.integers(10, 30)))

def add_typos(text, rng, rate=0.3):
    out = []
    for ch in text:
        r = rng.random()
        if ch.isalpha() and r < rate:
            op = rng.integers(3)
            if op == 0:
                continue                        # delete
            elif op == 1:
                out.append(rng.choice(LETTERS))  # substitute
            else:
                out.append(ch + rng.choice(LETTERS))  # insert
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return "".join(out)

def make_dirty_benchmark(df, seed=7):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    d = df[["Class Index", "Title", "Description"]].copy().reset_index(drop=True).astype({"Class Index": object})
    n = len(d)
    pool = list(rng.permutation(n))
    truth = {}

    def take(name, frac):
        k = int(round(frac * n))
        rows = [pool.pop() for _ in range(k)]
        truth[name] = rows
        return rows

    for r in take("label_flip", 0.05):
        d.at[r, "Class Index"] = int(rng.choice([c for c in (1, 2, 3, 4) if c != d.at[r, "Class Index"]]))
    for r in take("missing_title", 0.03):
        d.at[r, "Title"] = np.nan
    for r in take("placeholder_title", 0.005):
        d.at[r, "Title"] = "N/A"
    for r in take("missing_description", 0.02):
        d.at[r, "Description"] = np.nan
    for r in take("blank_description", 0.01):
        d.at[r, "Description"] = "   "
    for r in take("gibberish", 0.02):
        d.at[r, "Description"] = gibberish(rng)
        d.at[r, "Title"] = gibberish(rng)[:40]
    for r in take("typos", 0.02):
        d.at[r, "Description"] = add_typos(d.at[r, "Description"], rng)
        d.at[r, "Title"] = add_typos(d.at[r, "Title"], rng)
    for r in take("off_domain", 0.01):
        d.at[r, "Description"] = OFF_DOMAIN[rng.integers(len(OFF_DOMAIN))] + " " + str(rng.integers(1000000))
        d.at[r, "Title"] = "Item " + str(rng.integers(100000))
    for r in take("html", 0.02):
        d.at[r, "Description"] = (f"<div class='story'><p>{d.at[r, 'Description']}</p>"
                                  f"<a href='http://www.example.com/news/{r}'>Read more &raquo;</a></div>")
    for r in take("truncated", 0.015):
        d.at[r, "Description"] = " ".join(str(d.at[r, "Description"]).split()[:2])
    for r in take("invalid_label", 0.005):
        d.at[r, "Class Index"] = [0, 5, "unknown", np.nan][rng.integers(4)]

    # duplicates are appended at the end, copied from rows nobody touched
    untouched = pool
    extra, kinds = [], []
    for r in rng.choice(untouched, int(0.02 * n), replace=False):
        extra.append(d.loc[r].copy()); kinds.append("exact_duplicate")
    for r in rng.choice(untouched, int(0.01 * n), replace=False):
        row = d.loc[r].copy()
        words = str(row["Description"]).split()
        del words[rng.integers(len(words))]
        row["Description"] = " ".join(words)
        extra.append(row); kinds.append("near_duplicate")
    for r in rng.choice(untouched, int(0.005 * n), replace=False):
        row = d.loc[r].copy()
        row["Class Index"] = int(rng.choice([c for c in (1, 2, 3, 4) if c != row["Class Index"]]))
        extra.append(row); kinds.append("conflicting_duplicate")
    d = pd.concat([d, pd.DataFrame(extra)], ignore_index=True)
    for k, kind in enumerate(kinds):
        truth.setdefault(kind, []).append(n + k)
    truth = {k: [int(x) for x in v] for k, v in truth.items()}
    return d, truth

dirty, truth = make_dirty_benchmark(test_raw)
print("benchmark rows:", len(dirty))
print({k: len(v) for k, v in truth.items()})
dirty.to_csv("sample_data/ag_news_dirty_sample.csv", index=False)
with open("sample_data/ag_news_dirty_truth.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(truth, f)
test_raw[["Class Index", "Title", "Description"]].to_csv("sample_data/ag_news_test.csv", index=False)
dirty.sample(8, random_state=1)

Recommended preprocessing pipeline¶

  1. Disguised missing values in 'Description': Convert blanks and placeholder tokens to real NaN before any other step.
df = df.replace(r'^\s*$', np.nan, regex=True)
df = df.replace({'n/a': np.nan, 'null': np.nan, 'none': np.nan, '?': np.nan})
  1. Missing values in 'Title': Text cannot be imputed meaningfully. Fill missing 'Title' with an empty string and rely on 'Description' for those rows; drop rows where every text field is empty.
df['Title'] = df['Title'].replace(r'^\s*$', np.nan, regex=True).fillna('')
  1. Missing values in 'Description': Text cannot be imputed meaningfully. Fill missing 'Description' with an empty string and rely on 'Title' for those rows; drop rows where every text field is empty.

  1. Missing values in 'Class Index': Rows without a label cannot be used for supervised training: drop them or send them for annotation.

  1. Labels outside the allowed set: Map them to a valid class if the mapping is obvious, otherwise drop the rows.

Issue details¶

[HIGH] Encoding / markup artifacts in 'Description'¶

Found 2116 rows with broken HTML entities (e.g. '#39;', '&'), 293 rows with HTML tags, 243 rows with URLs, 739 rows with stray backslashes, 1 rows with repeated punctuation.

Recommendation: Repair entities with html.unescape (after fixing bare '#39;' style entities), strip tags/URLs, replace backslashes with spaces and normalise unicode (NFKC).

[HIGH] Likely mislabelled rows (BiGRU classifier, confident learning)¶

The classifier confidently prefers another class for 762 rows (per-class thresholds {'World': 0.781, 'Sports': 0.814, 'Business': 0.745, 'Sci/Tech': 0.745}; 334 rows with under 12 tokens were not judged).

Recommendation: Review the top-ranked rows first. Relabel to the suggested class when correct, drop when ambiguous, or train with a noise-robust loss (label smoothing).

[HIGH] Anomalous / garbled content (character autoencoder)¶

Length-adjusted reconstruction error above the 99th percentile of clean AG News text: garbled strings, heavy typos, markup or content unlike news.

Recommendation: Inspect the highest-error rows; drop the garbage ones and keep genuine but unusual news.

[HIGH] Rows dominated by out-of-vocabulary tokens¶

Over 30% of the tokens are unknown to the reference vocabulary (mean OOV 5.5%). Typical of gibberish, heavy typos, other languages or code.

Recommendation: Inspect and drop garbled rows; if the text is valid but domain-specific, extend the vocabulary.

[HIGH] Same text with conflicting labels¶

Identical (normalised) texts appear with different labels.

Recommendation: Resolve by majority vote or manual review; drop the group if no majority exists.

[MEDIUM] Bag-of-words representation is extremely sparse¶

99.893% of the 7866 x 29280 document-term matrix is zero (about 31.4 distinct tokens per row). 54.3% of the vocabulary appears only once; 14524 words cover 95% of all tokens.

Recommendation: Keep sparse matrices (scipy CSR) for classic models, cap the vocabulary at about 14524 words with min_freq >= 2, and prefer dense learned embeddings for deep models.

[MEDIUM] Encoding / markup artifacts in 'Title'¶

Found 757 rows with broken HTML entities (e.g. '#39;', '&'), 154 rows with HTML tags, 133 rows with stray backslashes, 3 rows with spreadsheet error codes (e.g. #NAME?).

Recommendation: Repair entities with html.unescape (after fixing bare '#39;' style entities), strip tags/URLs, replace backslashes with spaces and normalise unicode (NFKC).

[MEDIUM] Unusually long texts in 'Description' (IQR rule)¶

95th percentile length is 301 chars / 45 words.

Recommendation: Do not drop them: truncate the combined text at about 52 tokens (95th percentile) and inspect the longest rows for concatenated articles.

[MEDIUM] Missing values in 'Title'¶

228 NaN; 38 placeholder tokens (e.g. 'n/a', 'null').

Recommendation: Text cannot be imputed meaningfully. Fill missing 'Title' with an empty string and rely on 'Description' for those rows; drop rows where every text field is empty.

[MEDIUM] Unusually long texts in 'Title' (IQR rule)¶

95th percentile length is 65 chars / 11 words.

Recommendation: Do not drop them: truncate the combined text at about 52 tokens (95th percentile) and inspect the longest rows for concatenated articles.

[MEDIUM] Missing values in 'Description'¶

152 NaN; 76 empty/whitespace strings.

Recommendation: Text cannot be imputed meaningfully. Fill missing 'Description' with an empty string and rely on 'Title' for those rows; drop rows where every text field is empty.

[MEDIUM] Exact duplicate rows¶

Identical rows inflate the weight of some examples and leak between train and test splits.

Recommendation: Drop exact duplicates, keeping the first occurrence.

[MEDIUM] Very short / truncated texts (< 3 words)¶

Too little content to classify; often the result of truncation or scraping errors.

Recommendation: Drop or send for review.

[MEDIUM] Near-duplicate texts (TF-IDF cosine >= 0.9)¶

104 near-duplicate pairs among 7676 sampled rows (rewrites or minor edits of the same story).

Recommendation: Remove near duplicates or keep them in the same split (group split) so validation scores are not inflated.

[MEDIUM] Disguised missing values in 'Description'¶

Empty strings or placeholder tokens are not counted by df.isna(), so they slip past naive checks.

Recommendation: Convert blanks and placeholder tokens to real NaN before any other step.

[MEDIUM] Disguised missing values in 'Title'¶

Empty strings or placeholder tokens are not counted by df.isna(), so they slip past naive checks.

Recommendation: Convert blanks and placeholder tokens to real NaN before any other step.

[MEDIUM] Labels outside the allowed set¶

Unexpected values: 0, 5, unknown.

Recommendation: Map them to a valid class if the mapping is obvious, otherwise drop the rows.

[LOW] ALL-CAPS text in 'Title'¶

Mostly upper-case rows look like headlines/boilerplate and create duplicate vocabulary entries.

Recommendation: Lower-case during tokenisation (already done by the recommended tokenizer).

[LOW] Duplicate text (after normalisation)¶

Same text up to case/punctuation but differing in other fields.

Recommendation: Deduplicate on the normalised text; if labels differ see the label-conflict issue.

[LOW] Missing values in 'Class Index'¶

8 NaN.

Recommendation: Rows without a label cannot be used for supervised training: drop them or send them for annotation.

[LOW] ALL-CAPS text in 'Description'¶

Mostly upper-case rows look like headlines/boilerplate and create duplicate vocabulary entries.

Recommendation: Lower-case during tokenisation (already done by the recommended tokenizer).

8.5 How many of the injected issues were found?¶

For each injected issue we check which detector should catch it and compute recall (share of the injected rows that were flagged). For the two deep learning detectors we also report precision and ROC-AUC, since they can raise false alarms on clean rows.

8.7 Applying the recommendations¶

The cleaner applies the plan in order: standardise disguised missing values, drop rows flagged by the deep learning checks, repair text, drop empty texts and invalid labels, resolve label conflicts, deduplicate, drop truncated rows. We measure how many injected problem rows were removed and how many clean rows were lost on the way.

8.8 An agent that applies the preprocessing automatically¶

Section 8.7 applied a fixed list of steps in one go. The preprocessing agent (dq/agent.py) does the same job more carefully, in a loop:

  1. Observe: audit the current data (profile, issues, quality score).
  2. Plan: take the next action from its library whose target issue is still present.
  3. Act: apply it to a copy of the data, but only if the total row loss stays under a budget (20% by default).
  4. Verify: re-audit; keep the change if the quality score did not drop, otherwise roll it back.
  5. Measure: at the end, train the same quick model on the data before and after and compare them on independent clean data.

Compared with 8.7 it adds the steps that were missing there: imputing missing text fields from the other field instead of dropping rows, majority-vote resolution of conflicting labels, near-duplicate removal, relabelling mislabels the classifier is very confident about (at least 90%) instead of deleting them, numeric imputation / outlier clipping / log transforms for tabular data, and advice on vocabulary size, sequence length and class weights. Every step is logged with what the agent saw, what it did, why the step helps, and the measured effect.

In [59]:
%%writefile dq/agent.py
"""Preprocessing agent.

The agent works in an observe -> plan -> act -> verify loop over the recommender's issues:

1. observe: audit the current data (profile + issues + quality score);
2. plan:    pick the next action whose target issue is still present;
3. act:     apply it to a copy of the data (respecting the row-loss budget);
4. verify:  re-audit, compare score / target issue / rows, keep the change or roll it back.

Every step is logged with what the agent saw, what it did, why that step matters, and the
measured effect, so the whole run can be explained and reproduced.
"""
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from .profiler import PLACEHOLDERS, combined_text, is_text_like, missing_masks, normalised_text, profile_dataset
from .recommender import build_issues, grade, quality_scores
from .text_utils import clean_text

MISLABEL_POLICIES = {
    "relabel_confident": "Relabel confident cases, drop the rest",
    "relabel_all": "Relabel every suspected mislabel",
    "drop_all": "Drop every suspected mislabel",
    "flag_only": "Only flag them (no change)",
}


@dataclass
class Step:
    action: str
    title: str
    status: str            # applied | rolled_back | skipped | advice
    observation: str       # what the agent saw before acting
    detail: str            # what it did
    why: str               # how the step helps the dataset / the model
    rows_before: int = 0
    rows_after: int = 0
    cells_changed: int = 0
    score_before: float = 0.0
    score_after: float = 0.0
    target_before: int = 0
    target_after: int = 0
    dims_before: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    dims_after: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    code: str = ""

    @property
    def rows_removed(self):
        return self.rows_before - self.rows_after


@dataclass
class Assessment:
    profile: dict
    issues: list
    score: float
    dims: dict

    def affected(self, prefixes):
        return sum(i.affected for i in self.issues if any(i.id.startswith(p) for p in prefixes))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def _dl_for(df, dl):
    """Deep learning results are keyed by original row id (the DataFrame index); map them
    to the current row positions so the recommender can use them."""
    if dl is None:
        return None
    pos = pd.Series(np.arange(len(df)), index=df.index)
    cur = dl[dl["row"].isin(pos.index)].copy()
    cur["row"] = pos.loc[cur["row"]].to_numpy()
    cur.attrs = dict(dl.attrs)
    return cur


def _ids(df, positions):
    positions = [p for p in positions if 0 <= p < len(df)]
    return set(df.index[positions])


def label_value_map(df, label_col, noise):
    """Class name -> the value this dataset uses for it (1..4, 0..3 or names), learned from
    the rows the classifier judged."""
    if noise is None or label_col is None:
        return {}
    given = df[label_col].reindex(noise["row"].to_numpy())
    pairs = pd.DataFrame({"name": noise["given_label"].to_numpy(), "value": given.to_numpy()}).dropna()
    return {n: g["value"].mode().iloc[0] for n, g in pairs.groupby("name")}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the agent
class PreprocessingAgent:
    def __init__(self, text_cols, label_col=None, valid_labels=None, vocab=None, label_noise=None,
                 anomalies=None, max_row_loss=0.20, mislabel_policy="relabel_confident",
                 relabel_confidence=0.90, allowed=None, near_dup_rows=3000, keep_snapshots=False):
        self.text_cols = list(text_cols)
        self.label_col = label_col
        self.valid_labels = valid_labels
        self.vocab = vocab
        self.noise = label_noise.copy() if label_noise is not None else None
        self.anomalies = anomalies
        self.max_row_loss = max_row_loss
        self.policy = mislabel_policy
        self.relabel_confidence = relabel_confidence
        self.near_dup_rows = near_dup_rows
        self.allowed = set(allowed) if allowed else None
        self.keep_snapshots = keep_snapshots
        self.snapshots = []   # (label, DataFrame) after each applied step, for step-wise impact
        if self.noise is not None:
            self.noise.attrs = dict(label_noise.attrs)

    # ---- observe
    def assess(self, df):
        prof = profile_dataset(df, self.text_cols, self.label_col, valid_labels=self.valid_labels,
                               vocab=self.vocab, near_dup_rows=self.near_dup_rows)
        issues = build_issues(prof, _dl_for(df, self.noise), _dl_for(df, self.anomalies))
        score, dims = quality_scores(prof, issues)
        return Assessment(prof, issues, score, dims)

    # ---- the action library: (id, title, target issue prefixes, destructive?, why, function)
    def actions(self, columns=()):
        L = self.label_col
        other_cols = [c for c in columns if c not in self.text_cols and c != L]
        return [
            ("standardise_missing", "Standardise disguised missing values", ["disguised_missing"], False,
             "Blank strings and placeholders such as 'N/A' look like data but carry none, and df.isna() does not "
             "see them. Turning them into real NaN gives every later step one consistent definition of 'missing', "
             "so they are counted, imputed or dropped correctly instead of being fed to the model as fake words.",
             self._standardise_missing),
            ("drop_useless_columns", "Drop constant and identifier columns", ["constant_", "id_"], False,
             "A constant column has no information, and an ID column lets a model memorise rows instead of "
             "learning patterns (a common source of leakage). Removing them shrinks the feature space.",
             self._drop_useless_columns),
            ("drop_empty_text", "Drop rows with no text at all", ["empty_text"], True,
             "A row whose every text field is empty gives the model a label with no evidence. It can only teach "
             "the model to guess the majority class.",
             self._drop_empty_text),
            ("drop_invalid_labels", "Drop rows with missing or invalid labels", ["invalid_labels", f"missing_{L}"], True,
             "Supervised training needs a valid target. Values like 0, 5 or 'unknown' would otherwise become "
             "extra fake classes, wasting model capacity and corrupting accuracy metrics.",
             self._drop_invalid_labels),
            ("impute_text", "Fill missing text fields from the other text field", [f"missing_{c}" for c in self.text_cols], False,
             "Throwing away a row because one field is empty also throws away its label and its other field. "
             "Filling the gap from the remaining text keeps the example, removes NaN values that break tokenisers, "
             "and keeps the class balance intact.",
             self._impute_text),
            ("impute_other", "Impute missing numeric / categorical values", [f"missing_{c}" for c in other_cols], False,
             "Most models cannot handle NaN. Median imputation is robust to outliers, the missing-indicator column "
             "keeps the information that the value was absent, and 'Unknown' keeps categorical rows usable.",
             self._impute_other),
            ("repair_text", "Repair encoding and markup artifacts", ["artifacts_"], False,
             "Broken entities like '#39;' and '&lt;b&gt;', tags, URLs and stray backslashes create junk tokens "
             "that split one word into many vocabulary entries (\"nation #39;s\" vs \"nation's\"). Repairing them "
             "shrinks the vocabulary, lowers sparsity and lets the model see the real words.",
             self._repair_text),
            ("resolve_conflicts", "Resolve identical texts with conflicting labels", ["label_conflict"], True,
             "The same text with two labels is a direct contradiction: the model is punished whatever it predicts. "
             "Majority vote keeps one consistent label; groups without a majority are dropped.",
             self._resolve_conflicts),
            ("drop_duplicates", "Remove exact and normalised duplicates", ["dup_rows", "dup_text"], True,
             "Duplicates over-weight some examples and leak between train and test splits, which inflates "
             "validation scores. Keeping one copy gives an honest evaluation.",
             self._drop_duplicates),
            ("drop_near_duplicates", "Remove near-duplicate texts", ["near_dup"], True,
             "Near duplicates (the same story with small edits) cause the same leakage as exact duplicates but "
             "are missed by exact matching.",
             self._drop_near_duplicates),
            ("drop_junk", "Remove garbled / off-domain rows", ["anomalies", "high_oov"], True,
             "Gibberish, heavy typos and non-news content (code, product listings, logs) are noise the model "
             "tries to fit. Removing them reduces vocabulary pollution and the risk of learning spurious patterns.",
             self._drop_junk),
            ("drop_truncated", "Remove truncated / too short texts", ["very_short"], True,
             "A two-word description carries almost no topic signal but still counts as a full training example.",
             self._drop_truncated),
            ("fix_label_noise", "Fix suspected mislabels", ["label_noise"], True,
             "Wrong labels teach the model the wrong answer and make its evaluation unreliable. Rows the classifier "
             "is highly confident about are relabelled to its suggestion; ambiguous ones are removed (policy "
             "configurable).",
             self._fix_label_noise),
            ("clip_outliers", "Clip numeric outliers", ["outliers_"], False,
             "Extreme values dominate means, variances and gradients. Clipping to the 1st-99th percentile keeps "
             "the rows but limits their influence.",
             self._clip_outliers),
            ("log_transform", "Log-transform skewed numeric columns", ["skew_"], False,
             "A log transform makes long-tailed features closer to symmetric, which helps linear models and "
             "neural networks train stably.",
             self._log_transform),
        ]

    # ---- action implementations: return (new_df, detail, cells_changed) or None when nothing to do
    def _standardise_missing(self, df, a):
        out, n = df.copy(), 0
        for c in df.columns:
            if not is_text_like(df[c]):
                continue
            _, blank, ph = missing_masks(df[c])
            mask = blank | ph
            if mask.any():
                out[c] = out[c].astype(object).mask(mask, np.nan)
                n += int(mask.sum())
        return (out, f"Converted {n} blank or placeholder cells to NaN.", n) if n else None

    def _drop_useless_columns(self, df, a):
        cols = [c for c, p in a.profile["columns"].items()
                if (p.get("is_constant") or p.get("looks_like_id")) and c not in self.text_cols and c != self.label_col]
        return (df.drop(columns=cols), f"Dropped columns: {', '.join(map(str, cols))}.", 0) if cols else None

    def _drop_rows(self, df, positions, what):
        ids = _ids(df, positions)
        return (df.drop(index=list(ids)), f"Removed {len(ids)} {what}.", 0) if ids else None

    def _drop_empty_text(self, df, a):
        return self._drop_rows(df, a.profile.get("empty_text_rows", []), "rows with no text")

    def _drop_invalid_labels(self, df, a):
        lab = a.profile.get("label") or {}
        return self._drop_rows(df, lab.get("missing_rows", []) + lab.get("invalid_rows", []),
                               "rows with a missing or invalid label")

    def _impute_text(self, df, a):
        if len(self.text_cols) < 2:
            return None
        out, parts, cells = df.copy(), [], 0
        for c in self.text_cols:
            miss = out[c].isna() | (out[c].astype(object).fillna("").astype(str).str.strip() == "")
            others = combined_text(out, [o for o in self.text_cols if o != c])
            fill = miss & (others.str.len() > 0)
            if not fill.any():
                continue
            # a short field (e.g. a title) gets the first words of the other field, a long one gets it all
            typical = int(np.nanmedian(out.loc[~miss, c].astype(str).str.split().str.len())) if (~miss).any() else 12
            words = max(typical, 6)
            out.loc[fill, c] = others[fill].str.split().str[:words].str.join(" ")
            parts.append(f"{int(fill.sum())} missing '{c}' values (first {words} words of the other field)")
            cells += int(fill.sum())
        if not parts:
            return None
        return out, "Filled " + "; ".join(parts) + ".", cells

    def _impute_other(self, df, a):
        out, parts, n = df.copy(), [], 0
        for c, p in a.profile["columns"].items():
            if p["missing_total"] == 0 or c in self.text_cols or c == self.label_col:
                continue
            miss = out[c].isna()
            if p["kind"] == "numeric":
                out[f"{c}_was_missing"] = miss
                out[c] = pd.to_numeric(out[c], errors="coerce").fillna(pd.to_numeric(out[c], errors="coerce").median())
                parts.append(f"'{c}' with the median")
            elif p["kind"] in ("categorical", "boolean"):
                out[c] = out[c].astype(object).where(~miss, "Unknown")
                parts.append(f"'{c}' with 'Unknown'")
            else:
                continue
            n += int(miss.sum())
        return (out, f"Imputed {n} cells: " + ", ".join(parts) + ".", n) if n else None

    def _repair_text(self, df, a):
        out, n = df.copy(), 0
        for c in self.text_cols:
            before = out[c]
            after = before.map(lambda t: clean_text(t) if isinstance(t, str) else t)
            changed = before.notna() & (before.astype(object) != after.astype(object))
            out[c] = after
            n += int(changed.sum())
        return (out, f"Repaired {n} text cells (entities, tags, URLs, backslashes, Unicode).", n) if n else None

    def _resolve_conflicts(self, df, a):
        L = self.label_col
        if L is None:
            return None
        key = normalised_text(combined_text(df, self.text_cols))
        grp = pd.DataFrame({"k": key, "y": df[L].astype(str)}, index=df.index)
        conflicted = grp.groupby("k")["y"].transform("nunique") > 1
        if not conflicted.any():
            return None
        out, fixed, dropped = df.copy(), 0, []
        for k, g in grp[conflicted].groupby("k"):
            counts = g["y"].value_counts()
            if len(counts) > 1 and counts.iloc[0] > counts.iloc[1]:
                majority = df.loc[g.index[g["y"] == counts.index[0]][0], L]
                out.loc[g.index, L] = majority
                fixed += len(g)
            else:
                dropped += list(g.index)
        out = out.drop(index=dropped)
        return out, f"Majority vote fixed {fixed} rows; dropped {len(dropped)} rows in groups without a majority.", fixed

    def _drop_duplicates(self, df, a):
        dup = df.duplicated()
        key = normalised_text(combined_text(df, self.text_cols)) if self.text_cols else None
        if key is not None:
            dup |= key.duplicated() & (key.str.len() > 0)
        ids = df.index[dup]
        return (df.drop(index=ids), f"Removed {len(ids)} duplicate rows (kept the first copy).", 0) if len(ids) else None

    def _drop_near_duplicates(self, df, a):
        pairs = a.profile.get("near_duplicates", {}).get("pairs", [])
        second = {max(p[0], p[1]) for p in pairs}
        return self._drop_rows(df, sorted(second), "near-duplicate rows (kept one of each pair)")

    def _drop_junk(self, df, a):
        ids = set()
        if self.anomalies is not None:
            ids |= set(self.anomalies.loc[self.anomalies["flagged"], "row"]) & set(df.index)
        ids |= _ids(df, (a.profile.get("text_sparsity") or {}).get("high_oov_rows", []))
        return (df.drop(index=list(ids)), f"Removed {len(ids)} garbled or off-domain rows "
                                          "(autoencoder anomalies + rows with over 30% unknown words).", 0) if ids else None

    def _drop_truncated(self, df, a):
        return self._drop_rows(df, a.profile.get("very_short_rows", []), "truncated / very short rows")

    def _fix_label_noise(self, df, a):
        if self.noise is None or self.label_col is None or self.policy == "flag_only":
            return None
        fl = self.noise[self.noise["flagged"] & self.noise["row"].isin(df.index)]
        if fl.empty:
            return None
        values = label_value_map(df, self.label_col, self.noise)
        confident = fl["p_suggested"] >= self.relabel_confidence
        if self.policy == "relabel_all":
            relabel, drop = fl, fl.iloc[0:0]
        elif self.policy == "drop_all":
            relabel, drop = fl.iloc[0:0], fl
        else:
            relabel, drop = fl[confident], fl[~confident]
        relabel = relabel[relabel["suggested_label"].isin(values)]
        out = df.copy()
        if len(relabel):
            out.loc[relabel["row"].to_numpy(), self.label_col] = relabel["suggested_label"].map(values).to_numpy()
        out = out.drop(index=drop["row"].to_numpy())
        # these rows are handled now, so they should not be reported again
        self.noise.loc[self.noise["row"].isin(fl["row"]), "flagged"] = False
        return (out, f"Relabelled {len(relabel)} rows the classifier is at least {self.relabel_confidence:.0%} sure about; "
                     f"dropped {len(drop)} ambiguous ones.", len(relabel))

    def _clip_outliers(self, df, a):
        out, n, cols = df.copy(), 0, []
        for c, p in a.profile["columns"].items():
            if p["kind"] == "numeric" and p.get("outliers_iqr") and c in out:
                x = pd.to_numeric(out[c], errors="coerce")
                lo, hi = x.quantile([0.01, 0.99])
                n += int(((x < lo) | (x > hi)).sum())
                out[c] = x.clip(lo, hi)
                cols.append(str(c))
        return (out, f"Clipped {n} values in {', '.join(cols)} to the 1st-99th percentile.", n) if n else None

    def _log_transform(self, df, a):
        out, cols = df.copy(), []
        for c, p in a.profile["columns"].items():
            if p["kind"] == "numeric" and abs(p.get("skew", 0)) > 2 and p.get("min", -1) >= 0 and c in out:
                out[c] = np.log1p(pd.to_numeric(out[c], errors="coerce"))
                cols.append(str(c))
        return (out, f"Applied log1p to {', '.join(cols)}.", len(out) * len(cols)) if cols else None

    # ---- advice that does not change the data but belongs in the training pipeline
    def advice(self, a):
        tips = []
        p = a.profile
        ts = p.get("text_sparsity") or {}
        if ts:
            max_len = int(np.ceil(p.get("combined_word_p95", 0))) or 64
            tips.append(Step("advice_representation", "Choose vocabulary size and sequence length", "advice",
                             f"The document-term matrix is {ts['sparsity_pct']:.2f}% sparse; {ts['vocab_for_95pct_coverage']:,} "
                             f"words cover 95% of tokens; 95% of rows have at most {max_len} words.",
                             f"Use a vocabulary of about {ts['vocab_for_95pct_coverage']:,} words (min_freq 2), truncate/pad "
                             f"to {max_len} tokens, and use dense embeddings rather than one-hot vectors.",
                             "A vocabulary that covers 95% of tokens keeps nearly all information while dropping the long "
                             "tail of rare words, and a sequence length at the 95th percentile avoids wasting computation on padding.",
                             code=f"MAX_VOCAB = {ts['vocab_for_95pct_coverage']}\nMAX_LEN = {max_len}"))
        lab = p.get("label") or {}
        if lab.get("imbalance_ratio", 1) > 1.5:
            counts = lab["counts"]
            total = sum(counts.values())
            w = {k: round(total / (len(counts) * v), 3) for k, v in counts.items()}
            tips.append(Step("advice_imbalance", "Compensate for class imbalance", "advice",
                             f"Largest/smallest class ratio is {lab['imbalance_ratio']:.2f}.",
                             f"Use class weights {w} in the loss and stratified splits.",
                             "Without weights the model is rewarded for favouring the majority class; weights make every "
                             "class count equally in the loss.", code=f"CLASS_WEIGHTS = {w}"))
        if any(i.id == "near_dup" for i in a.issues):
            tips.append(Step("advice_group_split", "Split by near-duplicate groups", "advice",
                             "Some near duplicates remain.", "Use GroupShuffleSplit with near-duplicate groups as groups.",
                             "Keeps copies of the same story on one side of the split so validation scores stay honest."))
        return tips

    # ---- the loop
    def run(self, df, on_step=None):
        """Runs the agent. Yields nothing; returns (clean_df, steps, first_assessment, last_assessment).
        on_step(step) is called after every decision so a UI can show progress live."""
        df = df.copy()
        n0 = len(df)
        first = current = self.assess(df)
        steps = []
        self.snapshots = [("start", df)] if self.keep_snapshots else []
        for aid, title, targets, destructive, why, fn in self.actions(df.columns):
            if self.allowed is not None and aid not in self.allowed:
                continue
            target_before = current.affected(targets)
            if not targets or target_before == 0:
                continue
            observation = (f"The audit reports {target_before:,} affected " + ("rows" if destructive else "rows/values")
                           + f" for this issue; current score {current.score:.1f}.")
            result = fn(df, current)
            step = Step(aid, title, "skipped", observation, "", why, rows_before=len(df), rows_after=len(df),
                        score_before=current.score, score_after=current.score, target_before=target_before,
                        target_after=target_before, dims_before=dict(current.dims), dims_after=dict(current.dims))
            if result is None:
                step.detail = "Nothing the agent can change automatically for this issue."
                steps.append(step)
                if on_step:
                    on_step(step)
                continue
            new_df, detail, cells = result
            removed_total = n0 - len(new_df)
            if destructive and removed_total > self.max_row_loss * n0:
                step.detail = (f"{detail} Not applied: total row loss would reach {removed_total / n0:.1%}, "
                               f"above the {self.max_row_loss:.0%} budget.")
                steps.append(step)
                if on_step:
                    on_step(step)
                continue
            after = self.assess(new_df)
            step.rows_after, step.cells_changed = len(new_df), cells
            step.score_after, step.dims_after = after.score, dict(after.dims)
            step.target_after = after.affected(targets)
            step.detail = detail
            if after.score + 0.05 < current.score:
                step.status = "rolled_back"
                step.detail += f" Rolled back: the score dropped from {current.score:.1f} to {after.score:.1f}."
                step.rows_after, step.score_after, step.dims_after = len(df), current.score, dict(current.dims)
            else:
                step.status = "applied"
                df, current = new_df, after
                if self.keep_snapshots:
                    self.snapshots.append((title, df))
            steps.append(step)
            if on_step:
                on_step(step)
        for tip in self.advice(current):
            tip.rows_before = tip.rows_after = len(df)
            tip.score_before = tip.score_after = current.score
            steps.append(tip)
            if on_step:
                on_step(tip)
        return df, steps, first, current


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- downstream impact
def score_downstream(d, text_cols, label_col, reference=None, seed=0, repair_inputs=False):
    """Trains a quick TF-IDF + logistic regression model on d and scores it: on a clean
    labelled reference set when one is given, otherwise with 5-fold cross-validation on d.

    repair_inputs=True applies the same text repair to the evaluation texts, as a deployed
    pipeline would do at prediction time after training on repaired data."""
    from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
    from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
    from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score
    from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold, cross_val_predict
    from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline

    def xy(frame):
        x = combined_text(frame, text_cols)
        y = frame[label_col].astype(object).where(frame[label_col].notna(), "missing").astype(str)
        return x, y.str.replace(r"\.0$", "", regex=True)

    model = make_pipeline(TfidfVectorizer(ngram_range=(1, 2), min_df=2, sublinear_tf=True),
                          LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, C=4.0))
    x, y = xy(d)
    if reference is not None:
        xr, yr = xy(reference)
        if repair_inputs:
            xr = xr.map(clean_text)
        p = model.fit(x, y).predict(xr)
    else:
        keep = y.map(y.value_counts()) >= 5
        x, yr = x[keep], y[keep]
        p = cross_val_predict(model, x, yr, cv=StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=seed))
    return {"rows": len(d), "accuracy": accuracy_score(yr, p), "macro_f1": f1_score(yr, p, average="macro")}


def downstream_impact(before, after, text_cols, label_col, reference=None, seed=0, repaired=True):
    """Trains the same quick model on the data before and after the agent and scores both on
    the same evaluation data. With a clean labelled reference set this measures real
    generalisation; without one it falls back to 5-fold cross-validation inside each version
    (then the cleaned data is also easier to predict, so the gain is optimistic)."""
    out = {"before": score_downstream(before, text_cols, label_col, reference, seed),
           "after": score_downstream(after, text_cols, label_col, reference, seed, repair_inputs=repaired)}
    out["method"] = (f"trained on each version, evaluated on {len(reference):,} clean reference rows" if reference is not None
                     else "5-fold cross-validation inside each version (optimistic for the cleaned data)")
    return out


def stepwise_impact(snapshots, text_cols, label_col, reference=None):
    """Downstream accuracy after each applied step (cumulative), to see which steps matter."""
    rows, prev, repaired = [], None, False
    for k, (label, d) in enumerate(snapshots):
        repaired = repaired or label.startswith("Repair")
        r = score_downstream(d, text_cols, label_col, reference, repair_inputs=repaired)
        rows.append({"step": k, "after step": label, "rows": r["rows"], "accuracy": r["accuracy"],
                     "macro_f1": r["macro_f1"], "change": np.nan if prev is None else r["accuracy"] - prev})
        prev = r["accuracy"]
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def steps_frame(steps):
    rows = []
    for s in steps:
        d = asdict(s)
        d.pop("dims_before"); d.pop("dims_after")
        d["rows_removed"] = s.rows_removed
        d["score_change"] = round(s.score_after - s.score_before, 2)
        rows.append(d)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def agent_script(steps, text_cols, label_col):
    """A plain pandas script that records what the agent did (for the report / reproducibility)."""
    lines = ["# Preprocessing steps applied by the DQ-Recommender agent", "import numpy as np", "import pandas as pd",
             "from dq.text_utils import clean_text", "", f"TEXT_COLS = {text_cols!r}", f"LABEL_COL = {label_col!r}",
             "df = pd.read_csv('your_data.csv')", ""]
    for k, s in enumerate([s for s in steps if s.status in ("applied", "advice")], 1):
        lines.append(f"# {k}. {s.title} [{s.status}]")
        lines.append(f"#    {s.detail}")
        if s.code:
            lines.append(s.code)
        lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def agent_markdown(steps, first, last, impact=None):
    out = ["# Preprocessing agent log", "",
           f"Score: {first.score:.1f} ({grade(first.score)}) -> {last.score:.1f} ({grade(last.score)})", ""]
    if impact:
        b, a = impact["before"], impact["after"]
        out += [f"Downstream model ({impact['method']}): accuracy {b['accuracy']:.4f} -> {a['accuracy']:.4f}, "
                f"macro-F1 {b['macro_f1']:.4f} -> {a['macro_f1']:.4f}", ""]
    for k, s in enumerate(steps, 1):
        out += [f"## {k}. {s.title} [{s.status}]", f"- Observed: {s.observation}", f"- Action: {s.detail}",
                f"- Why it helps: {s.why}"]
        if s.status == "applied":
            out.append(f"- Effect: rows {s.rows_before:,} -> {s.rows_after:,}, score {s.score_before:.1f} -> "
                       f"{s.score_after:.1f}, affected {s.target_before:,} -> {s.target_after:,}")
        out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out)

Does the preprocessing help a model trained on the data?¶

A quality score is only a proxy, so we measure the effect on an actual model. We train the same quick model (TF-IDF with unigrams and bigrams + logistic regression) on four versions of the benchmark and evaluate every one on the same 5,000 clean rows from the AG News training set (rows whose text does not appear in the test set, so they are independent of the benchmark):

  • the benchmark with injected issues (what you would get without preprocessing),
  • the output of the fixed cleaner (8.7),
  • the output of the agent,
  • the original, uncorrupted test set (the best we could hope for).

When a version was trained on repaired text, the evaluation texts get the same repair, as a deployed pipeline would do.

What the agent achieved, and how the added preprocessing steps help¶

On the data. The agent applied 10 steps and gave 2 pieces of advice in 24 seconds. The benchmark's quality score went from 86.2 to 99.6, and it kept 6,785 rows where the fixed cleaner of 8.7 kept 6,428. It removed every gibberish, typo, off-domain, truncated, invalid-label, exact-duplicate and conflicting-duplicate row. The biggest difference from 8.7 is how it handles the label flips: instead of deleting 91% of them, it relabelled 285 of the 380 flips back to their true class and deleted only 14% (the ambiguous ones). It also lost fewer good rows: 261 untouched rows (4.3%) against 330 (5.5%) for the 8.7 cleaner.

On a model trained on the data. The same TF-IDF + logistic regression model, evaluated on the same 5,000 independent clean rows:

Training data Rows Accuracy
Benchmark with injected issues 7,866 87.60%
Fixed cleaner (8.7) 6,428 88.32%
Preprocessing agent 6,785 88.62%
Original uncorrupted test set (upper bound) 7,600 88.82%

The agent recovers about 84% of the accuracy lost to the injected problems ((88.62 - 87.60) / (88.82 - 87.60)), while training on fewer rows than the dirty benchmark. A better model from less data means the removed and corrected rows were actively hurting it.

Which steps matter. The step-wise experiment answers this honestly. With 5,000 evaluation rows one standard error is about 0.46 points, so most single steps change accuracy by less than the noise. The one clearly significant step is fixing suspected mislabels (+1.18 points): wrong labels directly teach the model wrong answers. The other steps help in ways a single accuracy number on this model does not show:

  • Standardising and imputing missing values fills 494 empty fields from the other text field, so those rows (and their labels) keep a complete input instead of being lost to a naive dropna(), and stops 'N/A' from being learned as a word or crashing tokenisers.
  • Removing duplicates and near duplicates mainly protects the evaluation: copies in both train and test inflate validation accuracy, so this step makes reported scores trustworthy rather than higher.
  • Repairing encodings shrinks the vocabulary and removes junk tokens such as #39;. It did not raise the accuracy of this bag-of-words model (a consistent artifact is still a usable token), but it matters for pretrained tokenizers, readable outputs and smaller models.
  • Removing junk and truncated rows reduces noise and vocabulary pollution; its measured gain here is small because logistic regression is fairly robust to a few hundred junk rows.

The lesson for the presentation: label quality is what moved accuracy most; completeness and uniqueness steps make the data usable and the evaluation honest; validity steps make the representation cleaner.

8.9 Interpretation of the results¶

Classifier. The BiGRU reaches 91.97% test accuracy (macro-F1 0.920). Sports is the easiest class (F1 0.971); Business and Sci/Tech are the hardest (F1 0.888 / 0.895) and the confusion matrix shows they are mostly confused with each other. That makes sense: stories about Apple, Google or the Sprint/Nextel merger are genuinely both business and technology. The training curves show the model fits the training set quickly (train accuracy 98% at epoch 10) while validation accuracy flattens around 92.2 to 92.4% from epoch 5 on. Dropout, label smoothing, weight decay and the learning-rate reduction keep the validation loss from rising sharply, and early stopping keeps the best epoch (9). In the tuning grid, the larger embedding (200) and label smoothing both helped, and the lower dropout (0.3) was better than 0.5 at this training length.

Deep model vs classical baseline. TF-IDF (unigrams + bigrams) with logistic regression reaches 92.32%, so it is slightly (0.35 points) better than our from-scratch BiGRU. We report this honestly: on short news snippets with strong keyword cues, a well-regularised linear model on sparse n-grams is a very strong baseline, and a recurrent model trained from scratch without pretrained embeddings does not beat it. In this project the classifier is a means rather than the end: what matters is that it gives useful probabilities for label auditing, and it does (next paragraph). A pretrained transformer would be the way to clearly beat the baseline (section 10).

The recommender finds the injected issues. On the benchmark with 14 kinds of injected problems:

  • every rule-based check found 100% of its injected rows (NaN and blank/placeholder values, invalid labels, truncated texts, HTML markup, exact duplicates, near duplicates and conflicting duplicates);
  • the label auditor found 91.3% of the flipped labels (347 of 380), ROC-AUC 0.975. It flagged 762 rows in total: 50% of them are our flips and 66% have some injected issue. Most of the rest are real ambiguities or real label noise that was already in AG News (next point);
  • the autoencoder found all gibberish, 82% of off-domain rows and 57% of heavy-typo rows with 1.1% false alarms on untouched rows (ROC-AUC 0.983). Together with the OOV rule (over 30% unknown words), 100% of gibberish, typo and off-domain rows were caught. The two checks complement each other: OOV is best for misspellings, the autoencoder is best for text made of real words or symbols that simply is not news (code, product listings, log lines).

Real problems in the original AG News. On the unmodified test set the auditor flags 261 rows (3.4%). The top ones are clear examples: a story about Boston's archbishop closing churches labelled Sports, the Sprint/Nextel merger labelled Sci/Tech with the model saying Business, a Dow Jones/MarketWatch acquisition labelled World. Many flagged rows are Business/Sci/Tech borderline cases where both labels can be argued, which is why the recommendation is review rather than delete. The profiler also found issues in the raw data that a plain isna() check misses: about a quarter of the rows have broken HTML entities, 105 training rows sit in groups of identical text with different labels, 32 training rows also appear in the test set, and one row contains the spreadsheet error string #NAME?.

Effect of applying the recommendations. Running the cleaner with the default steps increased the benchmark score from 86.1 (B) to 98.8 (A): validity went from 69.8 to 98.6 and label quality from 77.7 to 100. It removed all gibberish, typo, off-domain, truncated, invalid-label and exact-duplicate rows, 91% of the label flips and 97% of the conflicting duplicates. The cost is 330 of 6,042 untouched rows (5.5%), mostly rows the label auditor flags as ambiguous. That is the precision/recall trade-off of the "drop" action. For a real project the better choice is to review the top-ranked rows or to use the "relabel" option. Rows with a missing title or description are deliberately kept (the other text field still carries the topic), and near duplicates are reported but not deleted, because the right fix is a grouped train/test split rather than deletion.

Limitations. The label auditor only knows the four AG News topics, so on other datasets only the statistical checks and the anomaly detector apply. The autoencoder's notion of "normal" is English news text. Severity thresholds and score weights are hand-set rules, not learned.

8.10 The Streamlit application¶

The cell below writes app.py. Run it with streamlit run app.py (or run_app.bat). The sidebar selects a data source (the benchmark above, the original test set, or any uploaded CSV), the text and label columns, and which deep learning checks to run. A navigation bar gives six sections:

  • Overview: the quality score dial, dimension scores, the top issues and how many of them the agent can fix;
  • Issues: every issue with its explanation, recommendation, code, example rows and the agent action that fixes it;
  • Preprocessing agent: settings (row-loss budget, mislabel policy, relabel confidence, allowed actions), a live log while it runs, then before/after scores, the score trajectory, one card per step with what it saw, what it did, why it helps and the measured effect, the dataset-level changes, the downstream-model comparison (optionally per step), and downloads (cleaned CSV, agent log, steps, report after cleaning);
  • Data profile: columns, missing values and missingness matrix, text and sparsity statistics, correlations;
  • Deep learning checks: suspected mislabels and anomalies with their scores;
  • Report & export: HTML / Markdown report, issues CSV and the recommended plan as preprocess.py.
In [64]:

def esc(x):
    return html.escape(str(x))


def badge(sev):
    return f"<span class='sev' style='background:{SEVERITY_COLOR[sev]}'>{sev}</span>"


def fix_action(issue_id):
    return next((a for p, a in FIXABLE.items() if issue_id.startswith(p)), None)


def ring(score):
    g = grade(score)
    return (f"<div class='ring' style='--p:{score:.1f};--c:{GRADE_COLOR[g]}'><div><b>{score:.1f}</b>"
            f"<small>quality score<br>grade {g}</small></div></div>")


def kpi(label, value, sub=""):
    return f"<div class='kpi'><div class='label'>{esc(label)}</div><div class='value'>{value}</div><div class='sub'>{sub}</div></div>"


def delta(a, b, fmt="{:+.1f}", good_up=True):
    d = b - a
    cls = "up" if (d >= 0) == good_up else "down"
    return f"<span class='{cls}'>{fmt.format(d)}</span>"


def run_dl_checks(df, text_cols, label_col, max_rows, do_labels, do_anom):
    """Runs the DL checks on (a sample of) the rows; results are keyed by the DataFrame index."""
    checker = load_checker()
    idx = df.index.to_numpy()
    if len(df) > max_rows:
        idx = np.sort(np.random.default_rng(0).choice(idx, max_rows, replace=False))
    texts = combined_text(df.loc[idx], text_cols).reset_index(drop=True)
    noise = anomalies = None
    if do_labels and label_col:
        noise = checker.label_noise(texts, df.loc[idx, label_col].reset_index(drop=True))
        if noise is not None:
            attrs = dict(noise.attrs)
            noise["row"] = idx[noise["row"].to_numpy()]
            noise.attrs.update(attrs)
    if do_anom and text_cols:
        anomalies = checker.anomalies(texts)
        if anomalies is not None:
            anomalies["row"] = idx[anomalies["row"].to_numpy()]
    return noise, anomalies, len(idx)


def audit(df, text_cols, label_col, valid_labels, max_rows, do_labels, do_anom, name):
    vocab = load_checker().vocab if text_cols else None
    prof = profile_dataset(df, text_cols, label_col, valid_labels=valid_labels, vocab=vocab)
    noise = anomalies = None
    n_dl = 0
    if text_cols and (do_labels or do_anom):
        noise, anomalies, n_dl = run_dl_checks(df, text_cols, label_col, max_rows, do_labels, do_anom)
    return build_report(prof, noise, anomalies, dataset_name=name), noise, anomalies, n_dl
